District heat to a network.basis: Vancouver: TELUS data centre heat to the TELUS Garden thermal energy system (BCUC Order C-1-13, 2013) — a development-scale system, not a city network. Elsewhere: Tallaght, Dublin, Amazon data-centre heat, operating since 2023 (Codema); Meta Odense → Fjernvarme Fyn (COP 4.5, 2020); Mäntsälä. Precedent search 15 Oct 2026.

van: heat sold to others is a BCUC-regulated thermal energy system (TELUS Garden: Order C-1-13); NEU credit for heat returned $32.59/MWh (By-law 9552 Sch. C)
edm: Alberta rule for selling heat not yet read; Blatchford: connection compulsory, net-zero buildings exempt (Bylaw C17943 s. 6, s. 8)

District heat to a network.visual: pipe route from the site to the network, homes within reach

Hospital or campus anchor.basis: Université Laval, Québec: supercomputer heat to the campus loop, 1,150,000 kWh/yr. Equinix Amsterdam exchanges heat and cold with the University of Amsterdam through an aquifer store (RVO, Dutch government). Precedent search 15 Oct 2026.

van: as district heat if heat is sold across a property line

unknowns: the anchor's heat demand and supply temperature

New district with the data centre as hea.basis: Westville, Frankfurt: a new quarter of about 1,300 homes planned with at least 60% of its heat from a Telehouse data centre (Mainova, utility, 2021); 2,400 MWh/yr reported in a 2023 best-practice overview (Bytes2Heat). Old Oak, London is proposed (OPDC: 'thousands of homes', about 95 GWh across five phases, 2026–2040; 9,000 is the homes the development will deliver). Tallaght is a new network but serves existing buildings. Precedent search 15 Oct 2026.
unknowns: who pays for the network (capital split)
heat density of a future district
New district with the data centre as hea.visual: massing of a future district around the site

Warming centre, refuge, clean-air room.basis: No case found of a data centre hosting a public warming, cooling or clean-air room or refuge. Nearest: Vancouver's 111 E 5th rezoning requires "an active, high-quality public realm interface" (City report, proposed); the reverse — data-centre heat warming a public pool — is built in Paris (Butte-aux-Cailles, 2017). Precedent search 15 Oct 2026.

van: people sleeping in it makes that part residential occupancy (Group C, BCBC 2024 definition); separations from the data centre not yet read
edm: same Group C definition (NBC 2020 / NBC(AE) 2023); separations not yet read

unknowns: whether it reaches the people most at risk (2021: 98% died indoors, 56% lived alone)
Warming centre, refuge, clean-air room.visual: room inside the building with its own street entry

EV charging hub.basis: No built case of a data centre sharing its capacity or site with public charging. The reverse is announced in the US: GPU pods at EV-charging sites using idle capacity (Xeal, Sep 2026, operator claim). Precedent search 15 Oct 2026. Here (30 Oct 2026 triage, applied 2 Nov 2026): chargers on the data centre's lot with their own new grid connection; the data centre has no spare capacity to set aside.

van: exempt from UCA Part 3 (MO M104; BCUC G-66-19, 2019)
edm: not defined clearly in legislation; status unclear; most parties saw no need for more oversight (AUC Distribution System Inquiry, 2021, pp. 60, 68)

EV charging hub.visual: stalls drawn to scale on the lot, charger count

Meanwhile uses on land held for growth.basis: No documented interim public use of land a data centre holds for expansion. Closest: sheep grazing an on-site solar park (LCL Gembloux, operator claim), not shown to be expansion land or public. Precedent search 15 Oct 2026.

Greenhouse.basis: Göteborg Energi runs a 130 m² proof-of-concept greenhouse on about 24 °C data-centre heat since 2024 (city utility). In Canada: QScale Lévis heat to a 12 ha greenhouse park, under construction (Québec government); a 3 MW proof of concept in Manitoba (operator claim). Alberta: studies only. Precedent search 15 Oct 2026.

van: greenhouse in industrial zones not yet read

Sewage heat as comparator source.basis: Vancouver NEU: 3.2 MW of sewage heat recovery, expanding by 6.6 MW (City of Vancouver). A comparator that competes with data-centre heat, not a data-centre opportunity.
Sewage heat as comparator source.visual: side by side with data-centre heat

Snowmelt on sidewalks and streets.basis: Holland, Michigan melts about 690,000 ft² of sidewalks and streets with 35 °C power-plant waste heat (City claim); no data-centre snowmelt found. Research 19 Oct 2026.

edm: an encroachment agreement for structures in the road right-of-way (Bylaw 12513): application $300–500, then a fee; over 0.3 m or 5 m² the fee is the owner's assessed land value per m² × the area encroached (2026 fee schedule); whether pipes under a sidewalk count as an encroachment is not confirmed; owners must clear adjacent sidewalks

unknowns: who owns pipes under a City sidewalk

Stormwater held for the neighbourhood.basis: Vancouver: 192 developments manage rainwater on site, about 7,400 L/s of peak flow held back (City claim, to Sep 2025); no data centre named; holding a neighbour's or the street's water is not described. Research 19 Oct 2026.

van: required on site (VBBL 2025 2.4.2.5); holding more than required is not addressed
edm: required on lots over 0.16 ha (EPCOR guideline; Bylaw 18100, now repealed by 19627: clause not re-checked ?)

unknowns: what holding back sewer flow is worth to the city
Vancouver: whether a harvesting tank counts toward detention (City guidance 2025); Edmonton: not yet read
Stormwater held for the neighbourhood.visual: a tank under the yard with the required and the extra volume

Emergency water for neighbours.basis: No private tank found serving a Vancouver or Edmonton neighbourhood; the City's 2018 memo names the gap but not private tanks. Research 19 Oct 2026.

van: non-potable firefighting water: no permit if unconnected and marked (DWPR s. 3.1(b)); drinking water makes it a water supplier with permits
edm: non-potable firefighting water: the building code clause is the same as BC (NBC Alberta Edition 3.2.5.7) and the Potable Water Regulation covers only drinking water; drinking water piped to neighbours would make it a private utility waterworks (Alta Reg 277/2003 s. 1(1)(l)) with an engineer-stamped design: a registration if it only passes on city water, an approval if it draws its own river water or ordinary groundwater (Alta Reg 276/2003 Sch. 1–2, Div. 5)

unknowns: tank volume: not yet verified (the fire-code standard has not been read yet)
Vancouver: whether the site is inside the City's seismic saltwater system

floor_area.name: Gross floor area
floor_area.formula: footprint × storeys; Vancouver fallback: area_m2 × round(hgt_agl ÷ 3.5–4.5 m storey height) from the 2009 footprint layer (or total_gross_area / BCA Gross Building Area where held)
floor_area.coef: Edmonton: total_gross_area field; Vancouver: BCA Non-Residential Inventory Extract (UBC Abacus, listed as "Commercial"): pos. 19 Gross Building Area, 7 Gross Leasable Area, 8 Net Leasable Area, 20 Basement Area (all ft²), 6 Storeys, 4 Year Built, 42 Type of Heating, 45 Type of Construction (A steel / B concrete / C masonry / D wood-steel), 48 Zoning; one row per building or part — sum per roll number; quarterly .txt; no areas for ad valorem properties (major industrial, utilities, schools, airports) → fall back to footprint × storeys; Vancouver footprints 2009 carry area_m2 and hgt_agl/avght_m/maxht_m, rooftype, len, wid — fallback at 60 (storey-height divisor assumed; buildings after 2009 absent); measured GFA from the City energy report: 555 W Hastings 788,192 ft² (73,225 m²), 1050 W Pender 303,283 ft² (28,176 m²), 900 W Hastings 133,714 ft² (12,422 m²), 111 E 5th 130,548 ft² (12,128 m²)

server_floor.name: Server (raised) floor area
server_floor.coef: share 0.75–0.87 from Qu EDM1 (15,712/18,000) and eStruxture VAN-1 (7,500/10,000)

it_load_outside.name: IT load, estimated from outside
it_load_outside.formula: hall floor ÷ m² of hall per MW: 290–630 (typical) or about 250 (high density); IT MW = hall area ÷ that figure (M95, 19 Oct 2026: aligned to the tool)
it_load_outside.coef: Tool: 290–630 m² of hall per MW (≈ 1,590–3,450 W/m²), five built Canadian halls, operator claims: eStruxture VAN-1 ≈ 290, Hut 8 Vault ≈ 557, Qu EDM1 ≈ 584, Cologix VAN2 ≈ 619, VAN5 ≈ 627 ( §2.7); high density ≈ 250 (NEXTDC S3, QScale, operator claims). Context, not used: RVO 2018 ≈ 500 W/m² of server-room floor ('an order of magnitude'); US federal measured 355–667 W/m² — older, lower-density rooms; LBNL models 186–2,325 m²/MW VAN5 (23 Nov 2026, sizing audit): about 627 m2 per MW uses the facility web page's 1.6 MW (arch_inv_cologixVan5Web); the spec sheet says 'Site Capacity 1 MW' (arch_inv_cologixVan5Sheet2026), which gives about 1,003 m2 per MW. Both operator claims; conflict kept. Without VAN5 the top of the built halls is Qu EDM1 about 584 m2 per MW.

it_load_claim.name: IT load, operator claim
it_load_claim.coef: 2–4 MW typical downtown colocation; 40 MW stated at 111 E 5th (applicant figure in RTS 19744); permit record: no MW stated anywhere; load traces are BC Hydro primary-service upgrade at 555 W Hastings (DB-2022-01818) and new BC Hydro room at 175 W Cordova (BP-2021-06112); Cologix VAN4: 4–6.5 MW (two Cologix pages disagree) [decision 30 Oct 2026]

it_load_actual.name: IT load, actual (range)
it_load_actual.formula: IT MW × 8,760 h × 0.4–0.6 for every yearly MWh in the tool (M95: aligned to the tool); the 0.20–0.60 utilisation band is context and is not applied
it_load_actual.coef: colocation server utilisation 0.21→0.35 (LBNL 2024); capacity utilisation 0.5 (LBNL); average ÷ servers' combined maximum ≈ 0.6 (Fan et al. 2007, real data centre); leased share proxy: Digital Realty Toronto occupancy 96.4%, 55.8 MW white-space (Q2 2025 supplemental p.24) — occupancy ≠ utilisation; measured whole-building ceiling (City energy report): 555 W Hastings site EUI 1.84 GJ/m² → 37.4 GWh/yr total, 32.5 GWh non-heat ≈ 3.7 MW average for the whole 73,000 m² tower, data centre and offices together — so the ≥3.7 MW of operator nameplate claims cannot all be running at once; 1050 W Pender 11.2 GWh non-heat ≈ 1.3 MW avg; 900 W Hastings 0.57 MW; 111 E 5th 0.45 MW (no data centre yet); Equinix 10-K FY2024 (public filing, other operator): cabinet utilisation = cabinet space billed ÷ total cabinet capacity "taking into consideration power limitations" — Americas 81% (116,700 of 144,100 cabinets, 107 IBXs), EMEA 78%, Asia-Pacific 75%, company 78% (79% in 2023); MRR per cabinet Americas $2,550/month; new IBXs built for power and cooling twice that of earlier ones; Vancouver is a leased-only Equinix metro; Calgary CL1–3 and Kamloops KA1 (2020 acquisitions) listed in Schedule III; CALIBRATION: Telia Helsinki snapshot ERF 0.75 and PUE 1.152 with 4.11 MW waste heat imply 4.8 MW actual against 24 MW IT nameplate = 0.20 (one day, hall partly built out) — the low end of the band should be 0.20, not 0.35

servers.name: Server count
servers.coef: 600 W per 2-socket server (2023); racks: 1.8–2.5 m² per rack measured in LBNL benchmarking (2007); Vertiv 42U rack 127 kg empty; Dell R760 36.1 kg (2U) ?

heat_rejected.name: Heat rejected
heat_rejected.formula: Q ≈ E_IT + electrical losses; idle floor 36% of max

heat_temp.name: Heat temperature by cooling type
heat_temp.formula: air-cooled 25–35 °C; liquid-cooled: the loop as a case pair, return = class supply maximum + 11–16 K: W32 (cooler) 43–48 °C, W40 51–56 °C, W45 (warmer) 56–61 °C
heat_temp.coef: 11 Nov 2026: cost of heat uses the loop COP capped at the realised 3–4.5; Lorenz figures from the W32 loop (5.9–13.0) shown only as a theoretical note (small lift; not reached by built heat pumps in the register).

liquid_capture.name: Share of heat captured in liquid
liquid_capture.formula: 0.57–0.75 cold plate (LBNL: 57–59 % typical, 67–75 % best; decided 30 Oct 2026, project decision); 1.0 immersion; air: judged
liquid_capture.coef: 18 Oct 2026 (project decision, heat items 1–7;: air cooling — still no capture share for a whole air-cooled hall. Reuse is shown 'possible with a change' (heat pumps on the chilled-water loop or chiller condenser) and the figure 'not yet known'. Evidence: Oró et al. 2019 (return air up to 47 °C, condenser up to 50 °C; ERF on a primary-energy basis 25–45% / ~55%, not ISO ERF); Požgaj et al. 2025 (108 kW hybrid; liquid removes ~70 %, so ~30 % to air, implied; ERF 0.78 in the 3G case with heat pumps, 0.86 in 4G and 0.88 in 5G without heat pumps); Ljungqvist et al. 2023 (theoretical upper limit with no heat pump, 0.50–0.66 at 13–18 °C); Yuan et al. 2025 review (Table 2 temperatures; its '50–70% recoverable' is cited to Singapore energy statistics — unsupported, not used). 13 Oct 2026: direct-to-chip 48–75 % (LBNL 2014; NREL), cold plate up to 94 % (Heydari 2024), hot-water cooled 80 % (Zimmermann 2012); air-cooled: no primary figure; the often-cited 97 % (Lu et al. 2011) describes electricity becoming heat, not capture — unverified at source. A water-cooled chiller plant rejects all heat to the condenser loop

cop.name: Heat-pump COP (Lorenz)
cop.formula: COP = η × T_lm,sink ÷ (T_lm,sink − T_lm,source), log-mean temperatures on both sides (sink supply/return; source in/out); η 0.40–0.50 for built systems (calibrated 13 Oct 2026), 0.50–0.60 upper bound
cop.coef: 11 Nov 2026: cost of heat uses the loop COP capped at the realised 3–4.5; Lorenz figures from the W32 loop (5.9–13.0) shown only as a theoretical note (small lift; not reached by built heat pumps in the register).

heat_captured.name: Heat captured at the boundary (E_reuse)
heat_captured.formula: E_reuse = IT electricity × liquid_capture (capture shares are shares of server heat, not of all heat rejected; O-13, 30 Oct 2026), measured at the data-centre boundary by flow × ΔT before any heat pump (ISO/IEC 30134-6 cl.5–6; EU Reg. 2024/1364 Annex II 1(j))
heat_captured.coef: This is the figure a data centre may report as reused energy and the numerator of ERF; the network-side figure after the heat pump (what Stockholm Exergi and Fjernvarme Fyn meter and bill, and what Danish tax law meters "ved udgang fra varmepumpe" with 3 × electricity deducted) is heat_delivered, not E_reuse. The two differ by COP ÷ (COP − 1) ≈ 1.3 at COP 4.2. Published "heat delivered" figures must be labelled by which boundary they use; where the source does not say, mark unknown.

heat_delivered.name: Heat available after heat pump
heat_delivered.formula: Q_out = E_reuse × COP ÷ (COP − 1) — network-side heat after the heat pump; the match takes min(Q_out, receiver demand)
heat_delivered.coef: CALIBRATION: delivered heat is receiver-limited, not source-limited, in every built case with a large data centre — Mäntsälä 20–30 GWh/yr from a ~15 MW DC (15–23 % of nameplate-continuous), Westville 2.4 GWh/yr PLANNED from a 35 MW DC (≈0.8 %, our arithmetic; operation not yet sourced), TELUS Garden 4.9 of 12.3 GWh available (40 %; 2013 design forecast, Order C-1-13); only Heerlen (520 kW DC into a 5GDHC network) ran source-limited at 54 %. Report this quantity as heat AVAILABLE after the heat pump; the match quantity is min(available, receiver demand); Odense DH output ≈ 1.3 × DC-side heat at COP 4.2 (Inspirationskatalog) matches COP ÷ (COP − 1)

hp_electricity.name: Heat-pump electricity
hp_electricity.coef: allocation rule stated; show two rules

free_cooling_hours.name: Free-cooling hours
free_cooling_hours.formula: count hours with T_outdoor ≤ threshold (18–27 °C inlet, approach +1.5 air-side or +12 dry cooler)
free_cooling_hours.coef: 18 Oct 2026 (sweep M30–M32;: full free cooling for an air-cooled hall (13 °C supply, ~18 °C return, ~10 K approach) only at ≤8 °C outdoors: 3,284 h Vancouver, 5,522 h Edmonton in the CWEC year (the project's count). CWEC 2020 edition (header CWEC2011 format, years 2000–2017), computed: Vancouver Intl air-side full free cooling 7,109 h at 18 °C inlet / 8,086 at 21 / 8,645 at 24 / 8,759 at 27; dry cooler to 30 °C liquid loop 7,675 h, to 40 °C 8,760. Edmonton Intl: air 7,614 / 8,046 / 8,412 / 8,661; dry cooler 7,846 / 8,754 / 8,760. Approach +1.5 °C air, +12 °C dry cooler (assumed). HDD18 from file: Vancouver 2,810, Edmonton 5,514 (design values 2,925 / 5,120)

pue.name: Power usage effectiveness
pue.coef: Manor Farm target < 1.30; 13 Oct 2026: US average 1.4 (2023, LBNL); global 1.54, North America 1.49, new facilities 1.48 (Uptime 2025, INDUSTRY SURVEY); no Canadian figure (NRCan: no sufficient survey); no source splits existing buildings from purpose-built — use 1.4–1.55

backup_hours.name: Backup duration
backup_hours.formula: usable kWh ÷ load; fuel ÷ burn rate
backup_hours.coef: UPS runtime about 1–2 min (hyperscale), about 5 min (colocation), 10–15 min (financial); generators take over in 10–20 s (vendor claims); 12 h fuel minimum (Uptime) and 24–48 h typical (operator claims)

flexible_load.name: Flexible share of load

licence_flag.name: Water licence required
licence_flag.formula: BC: yes for open-loop heat exchange (WSR Sch. A item 9). Alberta (Guide to Groundwater Authorization 2023 §6.2): open loop with no water loss and return to the same water body = Water Act "activity" → approval; different water body or any loss → licence; closed loop → none. Flow tier for the aquifer test: Q(m³/day) = heat_kW ÷ (1.16 × ΔT) × 24; a 1 MW loop at ΔT 5 K ≈ 4,100 m³/day → top tier

Directive (11 Dec 2018) sets the construction standards; Guide App. 2 aquifer-test tiers by daily pumping rate: ≤10 m³/day 2+2 h, no observation well, no APEGA report (§2.2); 10–35 m³/day 24+24 h, 0–1 obs well; 35–65 m³/day 24+24 h, 1; 65–265 m³/day 48+48 h, 1–2; >265 m³/day 72+72 h, 1–2 obs wells, full §2 report by an APEGA groundwater practitioner; maximum daily rate = lesser of test rate and Q20 (20-year sustainable yield); CSA C448 referenced for installation; temporary discharge needs the director's authorisation

existing_building.name: Existing building to convert
existing_building.formula: parcels with buildings whose use and age suit conversion (from the parcel tables), less what policy steers to other uses
existing_building.coef: Precedents: 515 W Hastings office → Bulk Data Storage (2023); Edmonton office → data centre (2009, 2011), warehouse → data centre (Qu EDM2); Vancouver Office Conversion Policy addresses residential conversion only; no official vacancy statistics in either city; floor load: offices 2.4 kPa above the ground floor, 4.8 kPa on ground-access floors and basements (NBC 2020 / BCBC 2024 Table 4.1.5.3); computer rooms excluded from the office row; ≈ 6.0 kPa used in US VA design (claim-level transfer): upper office floors would need strengthening; both views shown, dated: UK valuation note 2017 'not readily adaptable'; 2026 note: such buildings can take another use [decision 30 Oct 2026]

ambient_cover.name: Acoustic cover from the place
ambient_cover.formula: the zone pair sets what is allowed; a louder zone is the cover — Vancouver credits no ambient noise for equipment
ambient_cover.coef: Vancouver By-law 6555: quiet→quiet 55/45, activity→quiet 60/55, intermediate or activity→other 70/65 (day/night); background credited only for commercial premises. AUC Rule 012 road categories credit ambient but apply only to power plants and substations. Neither city publishes a road-noise map (traffic counts only). Edmonton Bylaw C14600 (ss. 19–22, at the property line): 50 dBA overnight next to homes, 60 next to non-residential uses; no ambient credit (bylaw14600; P-13, 30 Oct 2026)

interconnection.name: Closeness to networks and customers
interconnection.formula: distance to the nearest interconnection point and to customers; latency targets of tens of milliseconds
interconnection.coef: Why operators locate in cities: third-party (colocation) firms favour urban settings for buyer proximity (Pan Fang & Greenstein 2025); backbone networks are biased to cities that serve as interconnection points (Malecki 2002); edge latency targets of a few tens of ms, VR under 16 ms (Satyanarayanan 2017); internet exchange and customer proximity (JLARC 2024). Locations of internet exchange points in Vancouver and Edmonton not yet sourced; exchanges: Vancouver VANIX (78 participants, six connection points), UNM-Exch Canada-West (64), CSIX (16); Edmonton YEGIX (9) — operator-reported; fibre adds about 0.005 ms per km one way, small within a city; locations are not shown

zoning_status.name: Zoning: allowed, conditional or rezoning
zoning_status.formula: look up the district: outright / conditional (development permit) / not listed (rezoning or text amendment)
zoning_status.coef: Vancouver: "Bulk Data Storage" (s. 2) is conditional in I-2, I-1C, I-3 sub-area A and FC-2 only; not permitted elsewhere, including all commercial and mixed-use districts; CD-1 site-specific. Edmonton: no named use; the City treats large-scale data centres as Major Industrial (permitted IH; IM only where existing 1 Jan 2024); Minor Industrial permitted in BE and IM, and in IH only where it existed on 1 Jan 2024; in UI only on the NAIT Main Campus (Appendix IV, Sub-Area 2), limited to storage; in FD only as temporary outdoor storage; Direct Control site-specific; s. 7.20(3.3.2) may make an ill-fitting use discretionary

rezoning_price.name: What a rezoning takes
rezoning_price.formula: duration + application fee + levies and charges on new floor area
rezoning_price.coef: Vancouver: target ~15 months to decision (~1 year from fee to hearing); CD-1 fee $94,500 (elsewhere) or $226,300 (downtown/Broadway) + $1,590 per 100 m² under 8,000 m²; DCL industrial $112.87/m², mixed employment $211.54/m² (none if floor area does not increase); ACC $12.92–24.22/m² from 30 Sep 2026; CAC exempt for 100 % industrial after 30 Sep 2026. Also where the City attaches conditions (111 E 5th heat delivery) and residents get a say (579 submissions). Edmonton (2026 Planning and Development Fee Schedules, effective 1 Jan 2026): rezoning to an Industrial zone (BE, IM, IH, … DC/IND) $2,745 base + $340/ha; Direct Control — Administrative $7,930, Minor $7,930 + $0.62/m² buildable, Major $15,855 + $1.06/m² buildable (Major = significant change in character or intensity, comprehensive site planning with technical studies); plus a notification and engagement fee of $1,650 per component; development permit, non-residential new building $1,220 + $500 lot-grading inspection up to 500 m² GFA, + $1.20/m² above; building permit $11 per $1,000 construction value to $1 M, $10 per $1,000 above. Off-site levies (Facilities Bylaw 19340, consolidated 23 Apr 2024; Arterial Roads Bylaw 14380, consolidated May 2026) are charged as a condition of subdivision (and, for arterial roads, development permit) only within defined catchments, mostly new neighbourhoods and industrial areas; rates are set in a separate annual document (2026 Off-site Levies Approved Rates, not yet retrieved). Edmonton rezoning duration still not stated; Edmonton duration: rezoning target 160 calendar days (~5.5 months) for complex files, which include all Direct Control zones, if a pre-application meeting is held; 90 days for non-complex; very complex set at the pre-application meeting (Rezoning Application Complexity, 1 Jan 2024); actual April–June 2026: 147-day average, 70% within target (Processing Times page); then public hearing, typically every two weeks. Fire hall off-site levy (Bylaw 19340) 2026 rates per hectare at subdivision, held at 2024–25 levels: e.g. Mistatim Industrial $23,724, EETP $20,618, Northeast EETP $12,816, Blatchford $32,813 (range $12,816–42,032)

consultation.name: Consultation and rights that apply
consultation.formula: list the approvals an option needs that trigger Crown consultation, and the City commitments that apply; describe, never predict
consultation.coef: BC: Water Sustainability Act licence (own water source) → Province may consult; on-site generation ≥ 50 MW or groundwater ≥ 75 L/s → EA reviewable (data centres not listed); new utility works needing a CPCN → BCUC reviews whether the Crown consulted; City land → UNDRIP Call 1.18 first right of refusal; Call 2.3 'include this in permitting decisions' (a commitment, not a legal duty); local governments have no constitutional duty to consult. Alberta: Water Act licence or public-land disposition → waits on consultation (ACO); power plant ≥ 1 MW → AUC application, Indigenous groups in the participant program only in Category A or by AUC call (Category C); a thermal plant < 10 MW on private land is Category B (not ordinarily included); Alberta's 2013 policy (amended 2020) applies to Crown decisions on provincial Crown lands and excludes access to private lands where Nations have no right of access, so a private urban site triggers it only through a Crown approval such as a water licence; no Alberta equivalent of the BC Declaration Act found

people_affected.name: People within reach
people_affected.formula: dissemination-area population × share of the DA within each radius (noise, light, heat receivers)
people_affected.coef: 2021 census counts by dissemination area, spread evenly within each area onto a 100 m grid and summed within 200 m, 500 m and the sound distance: people, households, 65+, under 15, renter households, households spending 30%+ on shelter, people in low income (LIM-AT % × population). Randomly rounded; suppressed values count as 0

construction_time.name: Time to build and connect
construction_time.formula: planning and permits + construction + grid connection (often the longest)
construction_time.coef: 12–18 months per building; 2–3 years to operation; grid can add 12–36 months (JLARC; IEA); Vancouver rezoning ~15 months; Edmonton permit data give build times for non-residential permits since 2024; Edmonton permit processing (targets / actual average April–June 2026): development permit, commercial or industrial new building 90 days / 73 days (76% within target); building permit, commercial/industrial 120 days / 64 days (86%); excludes notification and appeal periods

reclaimed_makeup.name: Reclaimed water as cooling make-up
reclaimed_makeup.formula: V_rec = s × make-up, with make-up = evaporation × C ÷ (C − 1)
reclaimed_makeup.coef: C (cycles of concentration) 2–4 typical, up to 6 (FEMP/EPA); 4–6 run on treated municipal wastewater (US DOE-funded study, 2012; power-plant scale); s = share substituted, user-set 0–1; operator precedents 0.74–0.99 (Microsoft, operator claim); data-centre site water 0.32–0.36 L/kWh (LBNL 2024, denominator to confirm); Metro Vancouver will consider supplying reclaimed water case by case for industrial uses (UT-019, 2023); EPCOR Gold Bar already supplies treated water to industry (operator claim, no volumes); no Canadian data-centre case found

greywater_neighbours.name: Greywater available from neighbours
greywater_neighbours.formula: V_gw = residents within reach × 98 L/person/day × 365; used = min(V_gw × recovery, make-up)
greywater_neighbours.coef: 98 L/person/day residential greywater (National Academies 2016, US data); treatment recovery share not found (gap); cross-property sharing: no BC or Alberta rule text found; San Francisco permits district-scale systems serving two or more buildings (SFPUC)

treatment_energy.name: Electricity to treat reused water
treatment_energy.coef: e = 0.75–1.1 kWh/m³ greywater membrane bioreactor; 0.94–1.28 mixed wastewater (Arden et al. 2021, US EPA authors); ~4.6 kWh/m³ in one small blackwater plant (university report, low confidence); viable only where water + sewer cost ≥ US$2.38/m³ (greywater) or US$1.85/m³ (mixed) (Arden 2021, US 2020 dollars) O-19 (30 Oct 2026): arden2021 was unreachable in check 2 and its entry gives no table or page, so these figures are marked ? on screen.

blowdown_recovery.name: Blowdown recovered
blowdown_recovery.coef: one US federal test (GSA GPG-052, NREL evaluation, 2023): blowdown −53 %, make-up −16 %, cycles 2.8 → 4.9; US$46.8k installed; hard water, single site (30 Oct 2026: the cycles 2.8 → 4.9 imply blowdown −54 % and make-up −19 % at constant evaporation, our arithmetic; the measured −53 % / −16 % are kept.)

pv_roof.name: Solar on the data centre roof
pv_roof.formula: kWp = panel area × 0.16–0.20 kWp/m²; panel area = 12 m² × the number of 6 × 2 m panel rows that fit on the roof outside the plant and its clearances (1 m from the roof edge, an assumption; rows 0.5 m apart along, 1.5 m across); MWh = kWp × yield (horizontal to latitude tilt)
pv_roof.coef: 18 Oct 2026 (sweep M102): the register now matches the layout the Solar card uses pvLayout); the earlier roof area × 0.66 × (1 − plant share) × 0.70 formula is retired. yield, annual kWh/kWp (NRCan municipal values, ±10%, losses in a 0.75 performance ratio): Vancouver 892 horizontal to 1007 at latitude tilt; Edmonton 944 to 1244. A flat-roof array at about 15° tilt lies between the two, so the tool uses horizontal as the low end and latitude tilt as the high end. Edmonton yields about 6–24% more than Vancouver per kWp. Module density 0.16 kWp/m² (2014 median) to 0.20 (current) (NREL); module cover 0.70 of a flat roof at 15° tilt; 66% of large roofs suitable (NREL 2016); roof share taken by plant from the cooling module P-05 (30 Oct 2026): 128 / 159 kWh per m² of roof is our derivation, at the optimistic end (module density × whole usable roof). Yields (30 Oct 2026, corrects P-16): NRCan published annual values everywhere: Vancouver 892 (flat) – 1,007 (latitude tilt), 716 vertical; Edmonton 944 – 1,244, 989 vertical; the monthly table sums 0–3 kWh differently from rounding.

pv_facade.name: Solar on the facade
pv_facade.formula: MWh = south facade area × module density × vertical yield
pv_facade.coef: vertical (south-facing, 90°) yield, annual kWh/kWp: Vancouver 716, Edmonton 989 (NRCan municipal values). Vertical gives 71% of the latitude-tilt yield in Vancouver and 80% in Edmonton; in Edmonton a south wall yields more than a flat roof (989 vs 944), because of low winter sun. Replaces the interim 0.4–0.6 factor. No Canadian BIPV cost found (30 Oct 2026: these are the NRCan published annual values, used everywhere.)

pv_share.name: Share of the data centre's power from its own solar
pv_share.coef: worked check (roof areas assumed, not sourced): 1 MW IT site 1.4–4.8 %; 10 MW site 0.28–0.96 %; PV is a small share at data-centre densities; avoided carbon at the tool basis, NIR 2026 consumption intensity (2024): BC 18.1, Alberta 346.1 g CO2e/kWh (average factors)

pv_cost.name: Solar installed cost
pv_cost.coef: CAD 2.00–3.20/W under 100 kW; 1.90–2.40 for 100–250 kW; 1.68–2.22 above 250 kW (NRCan/IEA PVPS Canada 2024); O&M ≈ US$21/kW·yr, 30-yr life, 0.5–0.7 %/yr degradation (NREL, US)

battery.name: Battery storage
battery.formula: MWh = MW × hours (1–8, default 4); area m² = kWh ÷ 34 (19–49)
battery.coef: round-trip 85% (NREL ATB 2024); PNNL 2022 LFP, 2021 US$ installed: 1 MW 518.59/kWh (2 h) and 448.34 (4 h), 10 MW 461.15 and 410.70 — about 10% above the 100 MW figure of 385; 2030: 340.46 (1 MW 4 h), 311.11 (10 MW 4 h); RTE 83% at the transformer, 2,400 cycles at 80% DOD, 16-year life; 34 ± 15 kWh/m² across built sites (Reber 2023); fire-code basis in BC/AB (NFPA 855 adoption) unconfirmed | 19 Oct 2026: cost range CAD 467–627/kWh (NREL 2025 US$334, 2024$, to PNNL 2022 1 MW 4 h US$448, 2021$; US$ × 1.3978, no inflation adjustment); O&M 2.5–4% of capex a year; 15 yr; cost per kW-year at 5.6% real compared with the programme value (Electricity card)

genset_test.name: Generator testing emissions
genset_test.formula: energy = units × kW × test hours at load; × emission factors
genset_test.coef: testing ≈14.5 h/yr per unit, ~4 h at full load (AUC 27938-D01-2023, Amazon 25.6 MW, derived); Vancouver noise by-law exemption caps tests ≈15 h/yr; uncontrolled diesel 14.6 g NOx, 0.43 g PM, 706 g CO2 per kWh (AP-42 Table 3.4-1, upper bound for modern engines); Alberta exempts standby generators from environmental approval; Vancouver Noise By-law s. 4.1(c): a test is exempt from the noise limits at most once a month, daytime, up to 60 min, plus once a year up to 180 min, at no more than 80 dBA [decision 30 Oct 2026]

hvo_swap.name: Renewable diesel in the generators
hvo_swap.formula: Δ lifecycle CO2e = fuel energy × (CI diesel − CI renewable diesel)
hvo_swap.coef: BC approved fuel codes −7 to 131 g CO2e/MJ (RLCF-012, Apr 2026); stack CO2, NOx and PM stay about the same; fossil diesel reference CI to retrieve

borefield.name: Borefield as the data centre's heat sink
borefield.formula: L = heat to ground (W) ÷ q; boreholes = L ÷ 150 m; area = boreholes × 36 m²
borefield.coef: q = 12 W/m (base design, 1,248 m) to 19 W/m (economic optimum, about 760 m), both for the ground-only heat-pump system; the dry-cooler hybrid only reused 760 m (derived by dividing the 14.5 kW cooling load by length, not the heat rejected to the ground, which also includes compressor work; Zurmuhl et al. 2018 s. 3.1, 4.2.1–4.2.2, a 14.5 kW data centre, Ithaca, k 3.27 W/m·K; checked 18 Oct 2026); Edmonton design k 1.9 W/m·K (Alberta Geological Survey) → ~7–11 W/m (scaling is an assumption); ≈2 ha of borefield per MW rejected; 40 MW ≈ 0.8 km²; screening only — CSA C448 sizing and a thermal response test required; no Vancouver ground data found P-22 (30 Oct 2026): "about 2 ha per MW" holds only at 12 W/m; at 19 W/m it is about 1.3 ha, and at the 7–11 W/m used for Edmonton 2.2–3.4 ha per MW (our arithmetic, same 150 m boreholes on 36 m²).

ground_warming.name: Ground warming over 20 years
ground_warming.formula: from the share of heat put in vs taken out
ground_warming.coef: +4.7 K over 20 yr ground-only, +1.2 K with a dry cooler (Zurmuhl 2018, small field); about +3 K in 3 yr where 4.8 × more heat went in than out (Kindaichi 2018, field measurement) — a borefield only lasts if neighbours take heat back out in winter

btes.name: Seasonal ground store for neighbours
btes.formula: heat out = η × heat stored; boreholes = charge W ÷ 47–83 W/m ÷ 35–55 m
btes.coef: η 0.45 steady state (simulated), 0.32–0.56 measured years 3–10, 0.06–0.21 in years 1–2 (Drake Landing, Okotoks); a 0.9 MW data-centre design: 240 boreholes, 55 m deep, 3 m apart, 1,863 m², waste-heat use 77 → 96 %, ~17-yr payback (Li et al. 2021); heat-pump COP for the lift not given (gap)

ates.name: Aquifer heat store (open loop)
ates.formula: flow (m³/h) = MW × 1,000 × 3.6 ÷ (4.18 × ΔT); heat out ≈ 0.6 × heat in
ates.coef: 172 m³/h per MW at ΔT 5 K (assumption); injection ≤25 °C typical (Netherlands limit; no BC/AB limit found) — air-cooled data-centre heat (25–35 °C) may exceed it; recovery 0.6 (0.4–0.85), ≈ €300/kW at 2 MW (Barth et al. 2026); BC: water licence (WSA); Alberta: Water Act approval or licence + professional report

deep_geo.name: Deep geothermal heat
deep_geo.coef: Edmonton: ~90 °C at 2.5 km, 30–80 kg/s → 2.1–5.6 MWth average per well pair, $4.7–8 M per well (Majorowicz & Grasby 2021); licensed by the AER (Directive 089, 2025); competes with data-centre heat as a district source rather than cooling the data centre; Vancouver: not plausible for power, direct use unproven P-21 (30 Oct 2026): the return temperature is not stated; 2.1–5.6 MWth from 30–80 kg/s implies a drop of about 16.7 K, a return near 73 °C (our arithmetic ?).

tes_volume.name: Hot or chilled water tank
tes_volume.coef: 169 L/kWh at ΔT 6 K, 34 L/kWh at 30 K (3,600 ÷ (4.18 × ΔT) ÷ 0.85; corrected 2 Nov 2026, N-22: the 0.85 had been left out); ice ≈ 10.5 kg per kWh (latent heat alone gives 3,600 ÷ 334 = 10.8 ?); usable share 0.85 and tank heights are assumptions; costs too wide to use (IRENA range)

envelope.name: Buildable envelope
envelope.formula: max floor area = site area × FSR (or FAR) available to the data-centre use; height, setbacks and building-width limits from the zone
envelope.coef: Vancouver I-3 A: FSR 3.00 (bonus not open to storage uses), 18.3 m (30.5 m discretionary), side yard 7.6 m, max building width and depth 61.0 m, floor-to-floor ≥ 6.0 m ground / 4.0 m above; FC-2: FSR 1.00–5.00 by sub-area (6.50 at discretion), 10.7–22.9 m (to 51.8 m), side yards not permitted; I-2: FSR 3.00, 18.3 m (to 30.5–36.5 m); I-1C: FSR 6.00, 46.5 m. Vancouver counts plant floor space above grade (excluded only at or below base surface, e.g. I-2 s. 4.1.2(c)). Edmonton IM: 18.0 m, FAR 2.0, setbacks 3.0 m street / 6.0 m to non-industrial; IH: 30.0 m, FAR 2.0, min site 1.0 ha; BE: 16.0 m, FAR 1.6. Edmonton s. 5.70(1.9): ventilating equipment, mechanical penthouses, tanks and stacks have no height limit

component_space.name: Space for the plant
component_space.formula: Σ components (electrical yard and switchgear, UPS and batteries, generators and fuel, heat rejection, heat recovery, fire suppression, loading) × IT load × redundancy
component_space.coef: 18 Oct 2026 (sweep M30–M32;: cooling space is per MW of HEAT (servers × PUE), spares added when the plant is laid out; air cooling → air-cooled chillers with free-cooling coils, 16.4–30.5 m²/MW across Vertiv Liebert AFC and Airedale TurboChill DCS, basis Vertiv AFC FIZ135 at 19.3 (equipment study 29 Oct 2026; Trane TCA dropped: Trane says it works 'without relying on glycol or separate free-cooling coils'; a dry cooler cannot cool water below outdoor air, and air-cooled halls need ≥13 °C chilled water, NREL/DOE FEMP 2024); liquid cooling → dry coolers, 19.5–30.5 m²/MW (EVAPCO, Thermokey, Mark; manufacturer claims). Manufacturer claims per MW (equipment study 29 Oct 2026, range across makers compared): UPS 2.4–3.3 m² (Vertiv EXL S1, Schneider Galaxy VX, ABB MegaFlex UL; basis Galaxy VX), Li-ion batteries 1.0–1.8 m² for about 5 min (Vertiv EnergyCore Li5, 4 cabinets per MW; Delta LZH, 400 kW per rack; basis Vertiv), air-cooled chillers 16.4–30.5 m², cooling towers 4.7–16.5 m² (BAC Series 3000, Marley NC; basis BAC S3E-1222-07R), dry coolers 19.5–30.5 m² (EVAPCO 21.9, SPX Marley OlympusV 24.1–25.0 dry-rated; the tool sizes 24.5), heat pumps 5.6–15.1 m² per MW heat (Sabroe DualPAC 7xx, GEA RedAstrum/RedGenium at 60/80 °C; basis DualPAC 716-W; HeatPAC dropped, its document is not on the maker's site), CDUs 0.4–1.5 m² (10 units, 6 makers; basis Motivair MCDU-50); equipment only, without clearances; EPCOR transformer clearances 3.0 m door side / 2.0 m others; fuel room 2 h separation and 550 mm clearance (NFC 4.3.14); generator room 2 h (VBBL 3.6.2.8); loading (7 Nov 2026): Vancouver s. 5.1 rounding to the nearest whole number, one-half up; clinic as an Office Use (row 5.2.9 Class B, our reading); the data centre's floor includes its support rooms at 33 % (the safer reading)

hall_area.name: Room for the data hall
hall_area.formula: new: envelope floor area − plant space − support − ground-floor uses the zone requires; part of an existing building: the floor area offered
hall_area.coef: Vancouver I-2, I-3 and FC-2: no data storage at the ground floor except entrances; calibration: Burlington 3,710 m² of halls = 48–72 % of gross area; Cologix VAN2 (≈619 m² per MW) dropped: its 2 MW is site capacity, not IT load; the range is unchanged, VAN5 (≈627) sets the top [decision 30 Oct 2026]

size_fit.name: Largest size that fits
size_fit.formula: hall area ÷ area per MW (range); for part of a building, also capped by floor load, electrical service and heat-rejection space
size_fit.coef: LBNL prototypes 3.7–13.9 m² per rack → ≈186–2,325 m² per MW; Ark UP4 28 MW IT in 15,410 m² (three buildings); 111 E 5th ≤ 291 m² per MW (upper bound); Uptime 2024 average 8 kW per rack (industry survey); Cologix VAN2 (≈619 m² per MW) dropped: its 2 MW is site capacity, not IT load; the range is unchanged, VAN5 (≈627) sets the top [decision 30 Oct 2026]; by cooling type (project decision, 12 Nov 2026): air 560-640 m2 per MW (four built Canadian halls); liquid to the chip about 150 m2 per MW (Schneider RD99, maker's reference design, claim); immersion the same figure as a stand-in, density not sourced yet; shown beside every lot: RICS 2.5-4.0 kW/m2 net white space (250-400 m2 per MW), run at 400, not the default VAN5 (23 Nov 2026, sizing audit): about 627 m2 per MW uses the facility web page's 1.6 MW (arch_inv_cologixVan5Web); the spec sheet says 'Site Capacity 1 MW' (arch_inv_cologixVan5Sheet2026), which gives about 1,003 m2 per MW. Both operator claims; conflict kept. Without VAN5 the top of the built halls is Qu EDM1 about 584 m2 per MW.

floor_load_need.name: Floor strength
floor_load_need.formula: equipment load of the hall (racks, batteries) vs the floor's design load for its original use
floor_load_need.coef: NBC 2020 Table 4.1.5.3: office 2.4 kPa (upper floors), 4.8 kPa (basement and ground floors with exterior access); equipment and service rooms ≥ 3.6 kPa; office row excludes computer rooms; data halls designed for actual loads (4.1.5.1.(1)); data-hall values 7.2 kPa (US DoD) and 12 kPa (TIA-942 Rated-3) need the standard

fuel_on_site.name: Fuel kept on site
fuel_on_site.formula: generator capacity × runtime hours × fuel per kWh, against the limit per storage room for the storey it sits on
fuel_on_site.coef: NFC 2020 Table 4.3.13.4.-B (Class II): first storey 200 000 L per room; basement or above the first storey 20 000 L (tanks > 2 500 L) or 45 000 L (tanks > 20 000 L); tanks > 230 L in a dedicated 2 h room; fuel use 0.264 L/kWh at full standby load (Rehlko KD2000, G5-626 9/23 p. 2: 528.3 L/h at 2,000 kW; manufacturer claim; our arithmetic) ≈6.3 m³ per MW per 24 h; at part load 0.304 (75 %), 0.312 (50 %), 0.363 (25 %) L/kWh; up to 4 % more by volume with HVO/renewable diesel (project decision, 11 Nov 2026; was 0.263, one Cat model); Uptime ≥ 12 h on site; whether data-centre standby counts as "emergency generators" is for the authority to decide O-06, corrected 31 Oct 2026 (research agent,: NFC 2020 / NFC(AE) 2023 4.1.1.1.(3)(b) leaves out of Part 4 only emergency-generator tanks up to 2,500 L, which follow CSA B139 (paywalled ?); larger tanks, as at a data centre, follow Part 4, so the Table 4.3.13.4.-B limits apply to them. Shown: 12 h (Uptime minimum) and 24–48 h typical (operator claims), project decision, 30 Oct 2026.

flood_exposure.name: Flood exposure
flood_exposure.formula: floor elevation of the plant vs the flood construction level, for parcels in the designated floodplain
flood_exposure.coef: Vancouver FCL 4.6 m (GVRD datum, includes 1 m sea-level rise to 2100, 1:500-yr, 0.6 m freeboard); switchgear, electrical panels and fire protection not below FCL unless flood-protected (VBBL 2025 Div. B 2.2.10.3(2); hazardous or toxic substances not stored below FCL, 2.2.10.3(3)); main switchgear in industrial buildings at or above FCL (F014 s. 3.3) P-14 (30 Oct 2026): clause settled by reading the by-law (earlier cited as Div. C 2.2.9.3); counting generator diesel as a "hazardous substance" is our reading (?).
flood_exposure.unit: m above or below the flood level

vibration_rank.name: Vibration to neighbours
vibration_rank.formula: qualitative rank of how hard plant vibration is to isolate at each position in the building
vibration_rank.coef: VBBL 2019 / BCBC 2018 apparent STC 47 between dwellings and other spaces (STC 55 by elevator shafts) — airborne only, no equipment-vibration limit; isolator deflection rises with floor span (US government spec citing ASHRAE); ASHRAE Applications ch. 49 not read
vibration_rank.unit: ranked: slab on grade → long-span upper floor

service_class.name: Electrical service
service_class.formula: IT load × PUE → the utility service class and what it brings (second feeder, transmission, clearances)
service_class.coef: BC Hydro: above 6.5 MVA (12.5 kV areas) or 13 MVA (25 kV areas) a two-feeder supply may be required; 60 kV and above under transmission rules. EPCOR: primary service typical above 2,500 kVA; transformer clearances 3.0 m / 2.0 m; access road 4.6 m in a 6.5 m strip P-12 (30 Oct 2026): power factor taken as 1, so kW = kVA (our assumption ?); 2 Nov 2026: replaced by a band, MVA = MW ÷ power factor 0.90–1.0 (our band; server power supplies ≥ 0.95, ENERGY STAR Servers v4.0, src_fill_estarServers4; facility value ?).

receivers_nearby.name: Receivers within reach
receivers_nearby.formula: every candidate receiver whose straight-line distance ≤ its type's reach (receiver_radius); each carries its demand (disclosed, else floor area × intensity), the temperature its type needs, its profile, and where the record came from
receivers_nearby.coef: types: hot-water district network · ambient (low-temperature) network · steam network · pool · ice rink (also a source) · school · hospital or care home · housing · office · greenhouse · wastewater plant. Pools: water ≤ 37 °C by regulation, 25–28 °C recommended for competition pools (BC 2025). Ambient networks (Blatchford) take heat near ground temperature and lift it in each building. Hot water stored for taps must be at least 60 °C, and 49 °C anywhere in a recirculation loop (Vancouver Building By-law 2025 Book II, 2.6.1.12.(1), 2.6.1.1.(3)); so data-centre heat at 25–35 °C can preheat tap water but a heat pump or other source must finish it. Map records (15 Oct 2026, *.json): Vancouver 353 — 27 recreation centres, 1 arena, 20 hospitals, 103 care homes, 202 schools (StatCan ODRSF v2 records no separate Vancouver pools; recreation-centre contents not recorded) — plus 641 non-market housing projects (City open data); Edmonton 475 — 161 recreation centres, 23 pools, 22 indoor arenas, 13 hospitals, 2 care homes, 254 schools. 72 health records have no location and are counted, not placed. Arena ice plants are heat sources as well as receivers. | 20 Oct 2026 M87): care homes from each province's licence list replace StatCan ODHF care records. Vancouver: BC Residential Care Facilities, all licensed types inside the City (100 homes, 3,853 licensed places). Edmonton: Alberta continuing-care compliance reporting June 2026, latest visit per site since 1 Jul 2024, Continuing Care Home Types A and B and Group Homes (assisted living and lodges left out: BC's list has no assisted living); 159 placed by City assessment address (19 at the nearest house number within 20), 3 not placed (In and Out Home Care House #2, Shepherd's Care Kensington Village, Salvation Army Grace Manor). ODHF care records with no listed home within 150 m kept (Vancouver 7, Edmonton 1) | 20 Oct 2026 audit;: one lot, one count in both cities. Assessment estimates on a lot already holding a named receiver with its own figure, or at a StatCan hospital or care address, dropped (Vancouver 14, Edmonton 7: e.g. Mount Saint Joseph, BC Children's, Misericordia, Alberta Hospital Edmonton); schools inside an assessed building made tenants; same-name repeats on one lot merged. Estimate vs building-outline floor area: median 0.86 Vancouver, 0.65 Edmonton
receivers_nearby.unit: list: type, distance, demand, temperature, evidence

competing_sources.name: Other sources for the same receiver
competing_sources.formula: sources already serving, or planned for, each receiver: sewage heat recovery, wastewater plants, ice-rink refrigeration, other data centres, ground loops; a receiver whose demand is already met by a low-carbon source is a weaker match, not a missing one
competing_sources.coef: Vancouver NEU: 70% renewable, mostly sewage heat recovery, 6.6 MW added, 100% renewable target 2030 (City page, May 2025); Blatchford (Edmonton): ambient loop on geo-exchange and sewer heat. Ice rinks reject refrigeration heat — a source as well as a receiver. NEU By-law 9552 (2026): inside its service area, new buildings and major alterations must take NEU heat unless the City Engineer finds it not practical or economical (s. 2.1); heat returned to the network is credited at 50% of $65.172/MWh. Traced service area (2.3 km², ±45 m): 111 E 5th Ave lies inside, 70–130 m from the line — consistent with RTS 19744 making NEU heat delivery a material condition of that data centre

displaced_source.name: What the receiver uses now
displaced_source.formula: the heat source a match would replace: from the host-building question (gas boilers · hot-water system · electric baseboard · district energy) or the network's supply mix; carbon change = displaced heat × its factor − heat-pump electricity × grid factor, which can be zero or negative where the displaced source is already low-carbon
displaced_source.coef: factors from grid_co2 (NIR 2026) and the network's own reported mix; a network share described as "renewable" is the operator's word and is shown as such

hourly_overlap.name: Hour-by-hour match
hourly_overlap.formula: for each hour of the typical year: delivered = min(heat available, receiver demand); report the share of the receiver's annual demand met, the heat still rejected (surplus), and the receiver's peak that must be met without the data centre
hourly_overlap.coef: annual totals overstate the match: Vancouver heat demand is 47% in Dec–Feb and 2.5% in Jun–Aug (CWEC, computed); the data centre's heat is near-flat
hourly_overlap.unit: % of receiver demand met · MWh surplus · MW backup

workload_control.name: Who controls the computing
workload_control.formula: flexible load is offered only by whoever runs the workloads: a single-owner or hyperscale operator can shift its own computing; in colocation the building operator controls power and cooling, not the tenants' computing, so flexibility needs each tenant's agreement
workload_control.coef: business model from operator pages (claims) and permits; the learning-series EV and workload papers are models of single-operator fleets

commitment.name: How firm the exchange is
commitment.formula: existing = operating; committed = in a contract, permit condition or funded budget; planned = in a utility filing or adopted layout; proposed = an applicant or operator says so; possible = the tool found it and nobody has proposed it. Only existing and committed count as delivered
commitment.coef: states and rule set 14 Oct 2026 (learning-series critique); promised heat that is only possible is shown, never counted

futures.name: Futures
futures.formula: rerun the match in four futures: (1) as planned; (2) the tenant changes cooling — air ↔ liquid changes heat temperature, capture share and flexibility; (3) the tenant leaves — the receiver's backup carries its full peak and the building's reusable parts are listed; (4) the receiver leaves — all heat goes back to rejection, so full rejection capacity stays
futures.coef: lifespans from horizons (servers ~6 years, plant 15–25, network 40–50); closure cases in meta.lifecycle; three futures from the learning series; the fourth is our addition, labelled so [decision 30 Oct 2026]

property_tax.name: Property tax to the city
property_tax.formula: assessed value (land + taxable improvements) × combined class rate
property_tax.coef: Vancouver Class 6 (Business & Other): 12.4672 per $1,000 in 2026, of which the City 7.09436; Edmonton non-residential: 25.22 + 3.97 education = 29.19 per $1,000 in 2026; servers and computing equipment are not municipally assessed in Alberta; in BC whether servers are assessed is not settled (0)

tax_split.name: Who receives the tax
tax_split.formula: list the parties, not a sum: City / school (Province) / TransLink and licensed property records (local only) (Vancouver); City / education (Province) (Edmonton); then the City's spending shares
tax_split.coef: Vancouver: property tax ≈ 56% of City operating revenue, utilities the largest spending share (24%), police second (22%); Edmonton: "where taxes go" page

untaxed_equipment.name: Equipment outside property tax
untaxed_equipment.formula: per city, list what is and is not taxed: shell and land (assessed), computing equipment (Alberta: not municipally assessed; ≥ 75 MW provincial levy), BC servers (not settled)
untaxed_equipment.coef: Alberta Data Centre Levy from 1 Jan 2026 for ≥ 75 MW: (E + F) × R; E = 45% of cost of equipment under 4 years, F = 15% of older; R 2% on grid power → about 0.9% of new equipment cost a year; paid to the Province, creditable against Alberta corporate tax; Vancouver: no equivalent

afterlife.name: After the data centre
afterlife.formula: at closure, three streams: shell (reuse or demolition), equipment (stewardship program or disposal, with data sanitization), plant and batteries
afterlife.coef: Vacated first-generation centres "tend to remain unoccupied and are not readily adaptable" (UK VOA, 70); federal closures 500+ of 720; BC Recycling Regulation covers IT products (servers by interpretation, 60); Alberta designates computer equipment; large UPS batteries outside both consumer programs as read (gap); no official source on converting a data centre to another use; both views shown, dated: UK valuation note 2017 'not readily adaptable'; 2026 note: such buildings can take another use [decision 30 Oct 2026]

heat_flux_site.name: Heat given off per m² of site
heat_flux_site.formula: q = heat rejected at peak (W) ÷ site area (m²); shown beside the city value
heat_flux_site.coef: Vancouver peak grid-cell anthropogenic heat flux 119 (the highest single cell, not a city-wide value) (units assumed W/m²; Allen et al. 2011); Edmonton: no published value; US city-wide fluxes 10–75 W/m², about 1 °C of air warming per 100 W/m² at neighbourhood scale (cited in Sailor 2026); check: 10 MW over 1 ha → 1,000 W/m²

heat_plume_dT.name: Warmer air near the cooling units
heat_plume_dT.formula: at the coil: ΔT = Q ÷ (ρ·cp·airflow); at a neighbour: ΔT ≈ Q ÷ (ρ·cp) × (χ/Q)(x), a plume factor (dispersion method to be chosen with the Architecture mode spatial rules; air_screen_1h was dropped 30 Oct 2026); heat treated as a passive tracer (buoyant rise ignored)
heat_plume_dT.coef: airflow from manufacturer data (claim, 50); screening estimate, not a measured air temperature. Measured (first field study, Phoenix, 36–169 MW): downwind air 0.7–0.9 °C warmer on average, up to 2.2 °C, detectable 100–500 m away; condenser discharge 8–14 °C above ambient. Placement: units on the roof warm street-level air less than units on walls (Berlin model: up to 0.6 K for wall units, smaller for rooftop; Jin et al. 2020). The effect is strongest at night: Phoenix AC waste heat added more than 1 °C at night at some locations, little by day (Salamanca et al. 2014). A land-surface preprint (+2 °C) is context only

recirculation_flag.name: Warm air drawn back into the coolers
recirculation_flag.formula: flag when the coolers sit inside a roof recirculation zone — top of the units below Hc = 0.22R near the upwind roof edge (R = Bs^0.67 × BL^0.33, Bs and BL the smaller and larger of the building's upwind height and width) — or within R downwind of a taller neighbour, or next to a wall or screen that blocks their discharge; also when units sit at different fan heights or with gaps between banks
recirculation_flag.coef: wind alone cut a modelled bank's heat rejection to 83.5–89.5% of still-air (Duvenhage & Kröger 1996, peer-reviewed, numerical: cross wind starves up-wind fans; wind along the bank drives plume recirculation; higher fan platforms recirculate more); field cases 13.6% and 24% recirculation (1971, manufacturer engineers — claim); a hot roof warmed inlet air about 0.3 °C (Wray & Akbari 2008, 70); ASHRAE: recirculation can be a serious risk for units with intake and exhaust on one housing; much hotter roof-level air cuts condenser capacity; zone geometry approximate (Wilson 1979)

uhi_context.name: Urban heat in the area
uhi_context.formula: one line per city: the City's heat policy and action, and the measured surface heat island
uhi_context.coef: Vancouver: heat mapping, 30% canopy by 2050; Edmonton: Cool Edmonton (Action 9), hot days about 1 → 16 a year by the 2050s; surface heat island Vancouver summer day 7.25 °C, Edmonton winter night 2.86 °C (Duan et al. 2026); near data centres in Phoenix, surface about 0.5 °C warmer within 1 km and less vegetation, with low-income and minority neighbours over-represented (Molla 2026, exploratory, no causality); neither city regulates heat rejected by equipment

air_permit_trigger.name: Air permit trigger
air_permit_trigger.formula: Vancouver: daily NOx on a test day vs 5 kg/day (Bylaw 1082 s. 7(12)); Edmonton: emergency standby generators exempt from an EPEA approval (daily NOx = genset_test NOx factor × kWe × test hours; 30 Oct 2026, after genset_emission_rate was dropped)
air_permit_trigger.coef: a 2 MW generator at full load passes 5 kg of NOx in about 10 minutes (arithmetic, 60: whether s. 7(9) exempts engines outright is unsettled)

free_cooling_hours_2050s.name: Free-cooling hours in the 2050s
free_cooling_hours_2050s.formula: same count as free_cooling_hours, run on the PCIC 2050s file (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5); shown beside today's value
free_cooling_hours_2050s.coef: computed 19 Oct 2026 from the PCIC files (Vancouver Intl): hours ≤ 8 °C 3,284 now → 2,279 (SSP2-4.5) / 1,954 (SSP5-8.5); hours > 18 °C 1,085 → 1,879 / 2,218; peak 25.6 → 27.6 / 28.6 °C. Edmonton Intl: hours ≤ 8 °C 5,522 → 5,047 / 4,815; hours > 18 °C 914 → 1,259 / 1,479; hours ≥ 30 °C 0 → 22 / 71; peak 29.0 → 31.9 / 33.3 °C. Files shift averages ("Heat waves or cold spells remain largely unchanged")

homes_heated_2050s.name: Homes heated in the 2050s
homes_heated_2050s.formula: homes = heat available ÷ (space heat × HDD(2050s) ÷ HDD(now) + hot water)
homes_heated_2050s.coef: space / hot-water split from CEUD 2023 (BC 46.2% / 27.1%; AB 63.1% / 23.2%); space heat assumed ∝ HDD, hot water unchanged; computed from PCIC (daily-mean HDD18): Vancouver 2,755 now → 2,198 (SSP2-4.5, −20%) / 2,038 (SSP5-8.5, −26%); Edmonton 5,389 → 4,659 (−14%) / 4,377 (−19%); published (RCP8.5, not like-for-like): Metro Vancouver −25%, Edmonton 5,657 → 4,331

water_restriction_rule.name: Water restrictions in a drought
water_restriction_rule.formula: per city, text only: what each restriction stage asks of evaporative cooling
water_restriction_rule.coef: Vancouver: stages 1–3 do not restrict evaporative cooling; stage 4 asks industry for voluntary cuts; once-through cooling on City water banned at all times; towers need a permit and monthly Legionella reports. Edmonton: EPCOR stages target 5/10/15/25% cuts; stages 3–4 "must"; cooling towers reduced "where possible"; whether data-centre cooling is essential is not defined

restriction_history.name: Recent water restrictions
restriction_history.coef: Vancouver: Stage 2 from 1 May 2026, Stage 3 anticipated early June (Metro Vancouver report, 1 May 2026); 2023 the last escalation to Stage 2 before 2026; earlier dates held back until each is sourced (P-19, 30 Oct 2026); Edmonton: one mandatory ban 29 Jan–2 Feb 2024 (plant failure, not drought); EPCOR: restrictions not every year

importance_cat.name: Earthquake design category
importance_cat.formula: Normal (IE 1.0) by default; High (1.3) only for the types the code names (community centres and schools in NBC 2020 / BCBC 2024; the 2018 'likely post-disaster shelter' wording is gone), or if the owner designs to it voluntarily; post-disaster (1.5) if it serves as a communications facility, unless the authority exempts
importance_cat.coef: High raises seismic design forces 30% over Normal (ratio only, not cost); Vancouver's new seismic rules apply to permits from 15 Sep 2026; whether a data centre counts as a communications facility is for the authority (20)

seismic_sa02.name: Earthquake hazard
seismic_sa02.formula: Sa(0.2), 2%/50 yr, Site Class C, from the NRCan NBC 2020 hazard tool for the parcel
seismic_sa02.coef: NBC 2020 final, Site Class C: Vancouver (V09) 1.08, Edmonton (E05 0.152, E06 0.154): Vancouver about 7×

battery_code_path.name: Battery rules
battery_code_path.formula: grid battery (ESS): certified; not above 23 m or below the lowest egress level unless in an electrical equipment vault; outdoors ≥ 3 m from egress and ≥ 1.5 m from openings unless UL 9540A-evaluated; UPS batteries are not an ESS and follow the general battery rules (ventilation, authorized access)
battery_code_path.coef: CEC 2024 Section 64 (Rules 64-902, 64-926, 64-1002; Appendix B) published 4 Mar 2024; in force Alberta 1 Apr 2025, BC 4 Mar 2025 (Technical Safety BC, IB-EL 2024-01, 11 Jun 2024); no city fire bylaw adds battery rules in either city; NFPA 855 commercial thresholds stay reference only (unverified)

nations_named.name: Nations whose lands these are
nations_named.formula: the City's own wording, and links to each Nation's own referral page; no statement of any Nation's position
nations_named.coef: Vancouver: xʷməθkʷəy̓əm (Musqueam), Sḵwx̱wú7mesh Úxwumixw (Squamish), səlilwətaɬ (Tsleil-Waututh), unceded territories; Edmonton: Treaty 6 territory and the Métis homeland, peoples named, not individual Nations (Confederacy of Treaty No. 6 lists 15)

city_commitments.name: City commitments to Indigenous Nations
city_commitments.formula: commitments, not legal duties: Vancouver UNDRIP Strategy Calls 1.18, 2.1–2.3, 2.5, 3.10 and the Action Plan engagement framework (in progress); Edmonton Indigenous Framework roles and Urban Reserve Strategy
city_commitments.coef: Vancouver endorsed the Strategy 25 Oct 2022 and the Action Plan 25 Jun 2024; Edmonton has no land-use or rezoning commitment like Vancouver's (stated plainly)

vibration_target.name: Vibration limit at neighbours (reference)
vibration_target.formula: compare with reference criteria: 72 VdB homes at night, 75 institutions, 65 vibration-sensitive rooms
vibration_target.coef: US FTA criteria, transferred; neither city's noise bylaw mentions vibration; ISO standards set no neighbour limits

heat_value_split.name: Who keeps the value of the heat
heat_value_split.formula: describe who controls each share (operator, utility, end users); no numeric split
heat_value_split.coef: no study measures the split; peer-reviewed papers say it is negotiated and the utility holds the stronger hand; a numeric split stays a gap (0) — a gap the thesis could fill

power_bill_effect.name: Effect on household power bills
power_bill_effect.formula: by size and province, text only: a typical in-city data centre (≈ 2.5 MW) shows no measurable effect in any source; very large loads depend on provincial connection policy
power_bill_effect.coef: BC Hydro modelling (2026): one new 75–250 MVA customer changes all rates by +0.4 to +1.5% by F2036 with no threshold, 0 to −1.2% under threshold options; AESO (2025): whether large loads pay their fair share of transmission costs is still open; LBNL (2025): mechanisms and protections, no quantified effect

ev_repay.name: EV port repaid by
ev_repay.formula: kWh = port cost ÷ (public price − electricity cost)
ev_repay.coef: BC: $15,000 ÷ (28.28 − 6.79) ¢ ≈ 70,000 kWh (≈ 9,400 h at 7.4 kW); Alberta: no public rate found; utilisation not published (no Level 2 figure)

pv_lcoe.name: Rooftop solar cost per MWh
pv_lcoe.formula: (CRF(5.6%, 30) × capex + O&M) ÷ MWh a year, against the energy charge it avoids
pv_lcoe.coef: self-use offsets the energy charge (RS 2289: "offset their consumption"); demand charge not reduced (flat load); BC exports 10 ¢/kWh up to 100 kW per phase; Alberta micro-generation under 5 MW

clean_power_price.name: New clean power: price and route
clean_power_price.formula: BC: new supply only through BC Hydro calls; Alberta: a corporate PPA, physical or virtual, against the pool price
clean_power_price.coef: BC Hydro calls: $74/MWh (2024 call, 2024$; restated $76 in 2025$) and $82/MWh (2025 call, 2025$); only BC Hydro signs; no direct customer route found (retail access suspended in 2011, current status not confirmed); grid access for data centres bid as a premium of at least 10% on BC Hydro's charges (2026 Call for Demand). Alberta: pool $43.68/MWh in 2025 ($62.78 in 2024); wind earned $23.18, 46.9% below the pool — the risk a virtual PPA carries; Alberta PPA strike prices not published (gap)

condensate.name: Condensate from cooling coils
condensate.formula: coils condense only when air is cooled below its dew point; hours a year with outdoor dew point above 15 °C (the top of ASHRAE's recommended IT inlet range), from CWEC
condensate.coef: computed from CWEC: Vancouver 417 h, Edmonton 117 h a year with outdoor dew point above 15 °C, so little condensate from a data centre; the monthly average dew point peaks near 13 °C in Vancouver and 12 °C in Edmonton in July–August (ECCC normals, vapour pressure 1.5 and 1.4 kPa, converted); US EPA rule of thumb for offices 3–10 US gal a day per 1,000 ft² conditioned (about 0.12–0.41 L/m² a day), not for data halls; litres per kW of cooling not found (gap)

stormwater_volume.name: Stormwater held on the lot
stormwater_volume.formula: Vancouver: small site a 3,400–7,200 L tank; otherwise stage 1 = 15 mm × non-landscaped area, released at 5 L/s/ha, then 25 L/s/ha. Edmonton (lots over 0.16 ha): 375 m³/ha for the 100-year storm at C = 0.90 (507 for 200-year), released at 35 L/s/ha
stormwater_volume.coef: the lot area is used as the non-landscaped area (an upper bound); Vancouver's full engineered volume (Modified Rational Method, 2100 IDF, 10-year) is not computed; extra volume held for a neighbour or the street costs as a tank ($667–2,955 per m³, register rainwater); no dollar value of avoided sewer upgrades found in either city

snowmelt_area.name: Sidewalk kept clear by its heat
snowmelt_area.formula: m² = heat offered (W) ÷ design heat per m²
snowmelt_area.coef: Edmonton design 430–700 W/m² (NRC CBD 160, 1974: sheltered to very exposed); ASHRAE 2015 lists no Canadian city; Seattle, the nearest listed (27 snowfall hours a year), is used for Vancouver: 420–647 W/m² at the 99% level (snow-free area ratio 0.5 to 1), about 36 kWh/m² a year at ratio 0.5; low-temperature fluid works (Holland MI 35 °C, Klamath Falls 38 °C); snow (ECCC normals 1991–2020): Vancouver 36.6 cm a year, 7.4 days with snowfall, 8.2 days with at least 1 cm on the ground; Edmonton 126.7 cm, 54.7 days, 145.1 days; no data-centre snowmelt built (gap)

fire_water.name: Firefighting water for neighbours
fire_water.formula: a tank on the lot, non-potable, for the fire department after an earthquake; drinking water makes the operator a water supplier
fire_water.coef: BCBC 2024 and NBC 3.2.5.7 (Alberta uses the NBC Alberta Edition, same clause per the NFC(AE) cross-reference): every building has water for firefighting; a sprinklered building is deemed to comply; where city supply is limited, a supply on site may be needed, sized for at least 30 minutes of fire-department hose streams (NFPA 1142 and the ISO fire flow guide named; volume not sized: standards not read). Vancouver: sprinklers rely on the mains; the seismic saltwater system (DFPS) covers downtown, part of Kitsilano and to VGH and takes about 80 years to complete. BC DWPR: a non-potable, unconnected, marked supply needs no permit; drinking water needs construction and operating permits. Alberta: drinking water piped to neighbours makes it a private utility waterworks (Potable Water Regulation s. 1(1)(l)); a registration if it only passes on city water, an approval if it draws its own source (Activities Designation Regulation); Edmonton: NBC(AE) 3.2.5.7.(1) — for buildings over 3 storeys or 600 m², municipal supply at least 3,800 L/min at 140 kPa, or an on-site volume by formula [decision 30 Oct 2026]

rack_count.name: Server racks
rack_count.coef: 7.1–8 kW per rack average (Uptime Institute Global Data Center Survey 2024 p.10: 'the average of typical racks densities ... 8 kW'; 7.1 kW without 11 sites above 50 kW; industry survey); cabinet 0.6 × 1.2 × 2.0 m (Vertiv VR3300; five makers share the footprint); arrangement in rows with 1.2 m contained aisles is schematic

ups_modules.name: UPS modules
ups_modules.formula: n = ⌈P_IT ÷ module rating⌉, then redundancy: N+1 adds one, 2N doubles
ups_modules.coef: 1000 kW frame, 3.6 × 0.9 × 1.97 m (Schneider Galaxy VX, UL 1778 + CSA); the UPS carries the IT load ('computer loads' on UPS, cooling on generator-backed power: LBNL 2007, one site; where continuous cooling is required, some cooling is on UPS too — not modelled ?); N+1 and 2N as defined by a UPS maker (Fuji Electric); UPS modules are redundant capacity components (TIA-942); the set-up's spare-unit choice is applied

battery_cabinets.name: UPS battery cabinets
battery_cabinets.formula: n = ⌈P_IT ÷ cabinet power at the runtime⌉, ×2 for 2N
battery_cabinets.coef: 10–15 min runtime (FM 5-32 3.5.2.1, insurer guidance; project decision, 11 Nov 2026); Vertiv EnergyCore Li5, 31.1 kWh, 263 kW (0.6 × 0.75 × 2.0 m, drawn): 186.6 kW for 10 min, 124.4 kW for 15 min (our arithmetic from the stored energy); Delta LZH at these runtimes not held (?). Earlier: about 5 min runtime (backup_hours, colocation); 263 kW per cabinet (Vertiv EnergyCore Li5, 0.6 × 0.75 × 2.0 m, drawn) to 400 kW per rack (Delta LZH) for 5 min → range (manufacturer claims)

room_cooling_units.name: Room cooling units
room_cooling_units.formula: n = ⌈heat to air ÷ unit capacity⌉, then redundancy; heat to air = P_IT (air cooling) or P_IT × (1 − liquid share) (liquid cooling)
room_cooling_units.coef: the unit follows room_cooling_type — room units: Vertiv Liebert CW181 (60 Hz, CSA/UL 1995): 172 kW at 80 °F to 246 kW at 90 °F entering air with 50/64 °F water (System Design Catalog ©2024 Table 2.3 p.11; 'DB' read as return air for a downflow unit — our reading); 179 kW at the legacy 75 °F; above 90 °F not printed ?; 3.10 × 1.07 × 2.39 m; liquid cooling leaves the rest of the heat to air (Schneider WP 133); thermal wall: CoolLoop CA80 500 kW; in-row: CR050RC 73.7 kW with about 20% extra (Vertiv CRV catalog)

cdu_units.name: Coolant distribution units
cdu_units.formula: n = ⌈P_IT × liquid share ÷ CDU capacity⌉, then redundancy
cdu_units.coef: 1516 kW at a 4 K approach, 0.91 × 1.57 × 2.05 m (Motivair MCDU-50, manufacturer claim); liquid share from liquid_capture (0.48–0.75; WP 133 gives 60–90%); sizing the CDU on the heat in the liquid is our inference (no primary rule found ?)

cooling_units.name: Outdoor cooling units
cooling_units.formula: n = ⌈P_IT × PUE ÷ unit capacity⌉, then spares (N+1 / 2N)
cooling_units.coef: heat to reject ≈ facility power (servers × PUE, high end); unit capacity: air-cooled chillers with free cooling 1.489 MW (Vertiv AFC FIZ135); dry coolers 1.18 MW (24.5 m² per MW over a 12 × 2.4 m unit; EVAPCO 12 m unit rated 1.31 MW); hybrid coolers 0.67 MW (low end of 0.67–1.37, EVAPCO/BAC claims); tower cells 3.03 MW (BAC S3E-1222-07R); air-cooled halls get chillers, liquid-cooled halls dry coolers

generator_sets.name: Standby generator sets
generator_sets.formula: n = ⌈P_IT × PUE ÷ set rating⌉, then spares
generator_sets.coef: 2,000 kW sets when the facility load is above 3 MW (Rehlko KD2000), otherwise 1,000 kW (KD1000); data-centre continuous rating = standby (Rehlko); the sets carry the whole facility, cooling included (HVAC on generator-backed power: LBNL 2007, one site); generator spares as set up (N+1 default); testing (check 1, 30 Oct 2026): emergency power systems are tested monthly at ≥30% of rated load for 60 min and yearly for 2 h at full load (CSA C282, via a fire department summary; whether IT standby sets fall under C282 ?) (weyburnC282); fuel and exhaust (check 1, 30 Oct 2026): diesel tanks for generators fall under CSA B139, not NFC Part 4 (nfc2020_4313; B139 paywalled, not read ?); code-required emergency power installed to CSA C282 (bcbc2024_3275; paywalled); exhaust: keep away from building openings and air intakes (mvBylaw1329); exhaust height not set by any code read (?)

hall_layout.name: Data-hall arrangement
hall_layout.formula: racks in back-to-back pairs: cold aisle | rack 1.2 m | hot aisle | rack 1.2 m; room cooling units along the long walls with their service clearance in front; corridors and travel distance to the building code; capacity check, revised 11 Nov 2026 (project decision, one method for floor and racks): the layout runs on the building at the size tested (its own generator yard and footprint), places the racks that size needs (rack_count) spread evenly over every place a rack fits at rack + aisle spacing on the hall floors (the first holds the UPS and battery room), and flags only when they cannot be placed; the size itself is set by the floor test (size_fit: 637 m² per MW for hall, UPS and battery, conservative end). How the racks are spread is our choice (?). Superseded: racks counted with rows thinned to 2.32 m² a rack (Schneider WP 46, project decision, 30 Oct 2026) on the current size's building and reported as MW (339 1st Ave E: 500 racks, 3.6–4.0 MW, on a building only the 2.5 MW set-up leaves; at 4.0 MW the deeper generator yard leaves a 501 m² footprint that holds 270 racks)

hr_flow.name: Heat-recovery water flow

hr_flow.coef: network side ΔT 15 K (Vancouver NEU minimum) to 30 K (UBC operating ΔT); source side ΔT 10 K (DualPAC rating, 30 → 20 °C); Q = V × 1.16 × ΔT (heat_in_water; water 4.18 kJ/kg·K × 1,000 kg/m³ ÷ 3,600 = 1.16 kWh/m³·K, physics; a primary property table not yet cited ?)

hr_pipe_size.name: Heat-recovery pipe size

Remaining gap: cheapest pipe and best COP together at the low end, the base-share table, and the utility's return and overhead inside a price. Second check (econ_lonsdale_check): card $74-149 for an all-boiler loop brackets Lonsdale's $108 price. Superseded 13 Nov figure: $61-73 (45-55 % low)

econ_elec_price_ab.name: Commercial electricity, Edmonton (energy-type charges)
econ_elec_price_ab.formula: Alberta pool price 2025 + EPCOR SAS-TOUP energy charge + operating reserve 7.99 % × pool; demand and capacity charges excluded (as ECON.elec.edm)
econ_elec_price_ab.coef: 2025 pool average $43.68/MWh (AESO Table 1) + $2.50/MWh (SAS-TOUP $0.00250/kWh) + 7.99 % × 43.68 = $49.67/MWh; on-peak 2025 $52.15, off-peak $26.74; distribution access and demand charges per kW/day not included

econ_network_flh.name: District network full-load hours (annual heat ÷ diversified system peak)
econ_network_flh.formula: annual heat delivered to buildings ÷ diversified system peak (our arithmetic on the source table)
econ_network_flh.coef: Mississauga downtown DES (FVB 2023, Table 7): build-out 297,250 MWh ÷ 110.89 MW = 2,681 h (2,575 h on the summed phase peaks); phases 1,951-3,121 h. Customer side: diversity included (85 %, then between phases), distribution losses not included (with constant losses added at the plant the hours rise a little). Climate: Mississauga, between Vancouver and Edmonton (no weather file stated). Not used: Lonsdale 75,935 MWh ÷ 34.5 MW = 2,201 h, because its 34.5 MW is not defined as a peak; the NEU 72,700 MWh ÷ 38.8 MW installed = 1,874 h, because it is installed plant and the NEU is the check target . No cold-climate (Edmonton) network figure found (not yet sourced)

econ_lonsdale_check.name: Second district check: Lonsdale Energy (North Vancouver)
econ_lonsdale_check.formula: published system totals for a second sanity check of the card method
econ_lonsdale_check.coef: 2023: 75,935 MWh sold (or 74,453: conflict), 108 buildings, 8.24 M sq ft (about 765,000 m², about 99 kWh/m² sold), 14.7 km pipe, plant and equipment at historical cost $51.7M (distribution $31.7M, about $2,160 per m of pipe, mixed-year dollars, not today's cost), effective price $108/MWh. A gas-boiler mini-plant system with some heat pumps, unlike the NEU's sewage heat pump base: use it for capital per MWh and pipe per metre, not base share. Capacity 34.5 MW undefined

row_svc_exit.name: Service rooms off exits
row_svc_exit.formula: no service room, store, washroom, laundry or janitor room opens directly into an exit stair or exit passage

row_wet_dc.name: Wet rooms and data centre

row_zyard_res.name: Side yards beside residential

row_ftf.name: Floor-to-floor minimum by zone

row_gen_clear.name: Generators off the growing house and edge

row_chiller_roof.name: Chillers over bather rooms

row_chem_store.name: Chemical stores: size and separation

row_greenhouse_sun.name: Growing house sun face
row_greenhouse_sun.formula: growing house on the face nearest south, never north of a hall storey; sun positions by declination and hour angle (not a sun study)

row_fish_hall.name: Fish hall at grade beside the data-centre block
row_fish_hall.formula: fish hall at grade, beside the block footprint; never under the hall

row_guards.name: Guards on raised walking surfaces
row_guards.formula: guard where a walking surface is more than 600 mm above the adjacent level; 1,070 mm high

row_cv_entry.name: Conservatory entry and visitor washrooms
row_cv_entry.formula: entry and reception at least 20 m2, 2.4 m wide; visitor WCs by Table 3.7.2.2.-A from the public load (biome and propagation 2.8 m2 a person with a posted sign)

row_heated_edge.name: Heated public edge (heat cascade)
row_heated_edge.formula: a heated strip along the main-street face at least 1.8 m deep, with an edge manifold room of 5 m2 on a street wall or in the pool plant; heat taken by area x kWh/m2
row_heated_edge.coef: 1.8 m; 5 m2; Vancouver 36, Edmonton 596 kWh/m2 a year

lay_aq_rooms.name: Aquaponics program rooms
lay_aq_rooms.formula: greenhouse and fish hall sized together before any class room, at 111: 28; fish hall at least 37 m2, 4.0-4.9 m deep; ratio check; class rooms only under data-centre storeys

lay_cv_rooms.name: Conservatory program rooms
lay_cv_rooms.formula: display biome, propagation and class rooms drawn from the definition minimums, biome on its own roof

lay_hc_rooms.name: Heat cascade growing house flag
lay_hc_rooms.formula: flags where the growing house is drawn (storey, area, width, nothing above)

lay_grow_group.name: Growing rooms as their own group
lay_grow_group.formula: greenhouses, headhouses, biomes and production houses carry group grow (not public) so loads and comparisons read them as the boards do

lay_chem_door.name: Chemical store doors
lay_chem_door.formula: a chemical store opens to the pool or bath plant or outside, never into a public room, corridor or lobby

lay_chem_place.name: Chemical store placement flags
lay_chem_place.formula: flags a chemical store off an exterior wall, beside a public room or under or over a data-centre room; moves nothing

rule_a10_door_inside_lot.name: Exit door swing kept inside the lot (A10, Vancouver)
rule_a10_door_inside_lot.formula: an exit or street door may not swing past the lot line onto a street

a10_recess_depth.name: Exit door recess depth
a10_recess_depth.formula: depth ≥ door leaf width (the leaf at 90° stands perpendicular to the wall)

a10_recess_width.name: Exit door recess (alcove) width
a10_recess_width.formula: door width + 0.3 m each side (hinge jamb, leaf thickness, hardware); barrier-free latch-side clearance may need more (VBBL 2025 3.8.3.6 not read)
a10_recess_width.coef: door + 0.6 m (2.4 m for the 1.8 m street door; 1.5 m for a 0.9 m door)

rule_edm_door_swing_permit.name: Door swinging over an Edmonton street
rule_edm_door_swing_permit.formula: no code fail; a City Streets Development permit or encroachment agreement (flag exit-recess:not-covered)

room_teaching_kitchen_ref.name: Teaching kitchen reference size
room_teaching_kitchen_ref.formula: 2.8-3.7 m2 a student (600-800 sq ft for 20) x 12 participants = 34-45 m2; 56 m2 for the 600 sq ft room whole. Definition minM2 111.6 is NBC kitchen occupant density (9.30 m2/person x 12), indicative

room_dining_per_seat.name: Dining area per seat
room_dining_per_seat.formula: 1.39 m2 a seat (15 sq ft) casual dining: 12 seats 16.7 m2, 20 seats 27.9 m2; definition minM2 14.4 = NBC 1.20 m2/person x 12

room_shelter_rest_per_person.name: Day shelter rest area per guest
room_shelter_rest_per_person.formula: 3.75 m2 personal space x 16 guests = 60 m2; Alberta reception-centre guide 3.5 m2 gives 56 m2 minimum

room_headhouse_share.name: Headhouse share of the growing area (CV, AQ, HC)
