room_lobby_min_ref.name: Entry / lobby sourced floor
room_lobby_min_ref.formula: VA lobby minimum 150 NSF = 14.0 m2; definitions keep 20 m2 (RULES.lobby.m2, drawing choice) above it

room_spa_rest_ref.name: Spa rest area
room_spa_rest_ref.formula: 40 spa bathers x one third resting (our guess) x 1.86 m2 = about 25 m2

rule_truck_class_b_bay.name: Loading bay, Vancouver Class B

row_change_rooms.formula: public-side change rooms (women, men, universal) at least 0.9 x the core's allowance; fail where fewer
row_change_rooms.coef: Vancouver / Edmonton, m2 incl. universal 19.4: community pool full 124.4 / 138.4, compact 80.4 / 81.4; warm bath full 69.4 / 83.4, compact 60.4 / 70.4; heat cascade 62 / 62 (spa-only), compact 56 (unchanged). Dressing area 0.32 m2 a bather (BC Guidelines for Pool Design v3, 2025, s. 5.1 p. 21; s. 8.7 p. 34) and 0.5 m2 a male and 0.5 m2 a female bather (NBC 2023 Alberta Edition Div. B 7.2.4.1-7.2.4.8); showers, WCs and 10 m2 a room for circulation are project arithmetic (ENGINE_SPEC_C4C5, 16 Nov); universal change room 19.4 m2 (17 Nov ruling). (24 Nov)

heat_recovery_room.name: Heat-recovery room (data-centre side)
heat_recovery_room.formula: one shared room on storey 1, data-centre side, beside freight lift E2, where the data-centre loop hands heat to the public side (heat pump); every typology that takes heat
heat_recovery_room.coef: 25 m², or 5.6 m² a MW where larger (pool_hrr), 3.2 m wide (the 339 pool board's 25.0 m², judged, not a minimum; main 14 Nov); wet room: not over UPS, battery, MV, meet-me, NOC or data rooms

front_garden_heat.name: Heated front garden
front_garden_heat.formula: garden m² × design heat per m² (kept snow-free); yearly MWh = m² × yearly kWh per m² ÷ 1,000
front_garden_heat.coef: Vancouver 420-647 W/m² design and about 36 kWh/m² a year at snow-free ratio 0.5 (ASHRAE 2015 ch. 51, Seattle as the nearest listed city); Edmonton 430-700 W/m² design (NRC CBD 160) and about 596 kWh/m² a year (ASHRAE 2023 ch. 52 Table 3, Minneapolis, melting 32.6 + idling 563.0; a US stand-in, not yet picked by project decision)

roof_terrace.name: Roof terrace over public parts
roof_terrace.formula: a lower roof over public rooms only (never over nothing-above rooms or the data-centre side), offered where a storey with its own public core (two stairs and a lift) touches it
roof_terrace.coef: at least 20 m²; a public floor above grade needs its own public core (hub rule, REBUILD_hub 23 Nov); barrier-free access by that lift

row_public_program_10.name: Public program at least 10 % of the floor
row_public_program_10.formula: public program (public-program + clinic zones) / the layout floor x 100 >= 10; support, circulation and cores not counted; judged (a layout under it is not kept)
row_public_program_10.coef: 10 % (project decision; judged in the export from 24 Nov)

row_plant_setback.name: Plant outside the setbacks (yards)
row_plant_setback.formula: every plant item at grade (generators, pads, chillers, dry coolers) at least the yard depth from each lot line that has a yard; exact rectangle-to-line distance; judged
row_plant_setback.coef: the zone's yard depths as the site model reads them (e.g. Vancouver I-3 sub-area A side yard 7.6 m, rear 3.1 m)

row_deck_access.name: Deck reached only through a change room (pool, bath)
row_deck_access.formula: every door of the pool or spa hall leads to the change rooms (wet side), a first-aid room of about 9.3 m2, or outside (exit); never a lobby, corridor or dry room; judged
row_deck_access.coef: 11 Nov rule; REBUILD_pool s. 1 (first aid keeps its deck door); design spec rule 6 (deck exits outside allowed)

flag_garden_generator.name: Generators within 3.0 m of the heated front garden (flag)
flag_garden_generator.formula: distance from each generator at grade to the heated front garden; under 3.0 m = flag for a later design stage (not judged: the 3.0 m vent reading is for room openings)
flag_garden_generator.coef: 3.0 m (the row_gen_clear distance, read as a flag here; project decision)

rule_scheme_u_flex.name: Storey-2 public flex where it fits (scheme U)
rule_scheme_u_flex.formula: after a cell's best layout is found, the same cell is searched in scheme U (storey 2 in front of the 2 h line is public program and flexible space, public stairs P1 / P2 and lift E1 from the street); a clean U layout replaces it, MW cost accepted; else the storey-2 remaining stays data-centre side, labelled "Flexible shell"
rule_scheme_u_flex.coef: project decision (and 23cd, 99, 109); sample: 6 of 104 layouts, 3 of 35 on the worst-remaining test

rule_compact_cores.name: Compact cores beside the full ones (compact twins)
rule_compact_cores.formula: every kept cell whose typology has a compact core also runs with that core (its own family + compact); high density is tried on every cell
rule_compact_cores.coef: compact cores: hub, learner pool and spa-only bath (COMPACT_POOL_answer), heat cascade (project decision), conservatory 186 m2 biome (project decision), food hub without greenhouse; project decision

rule_noise_empty_lot.name: Noise: an empty lot never binds
rule_noise_empty_lot.formula: the night limit is checked at occupied receivers only; where the loudest neighbour is an empty lot it is named ("limiting neighbour is an empty lot; next occupied neighbour used") and the next occupied receiver binds
rule_noise_empty_lot.coef: project decision; By-law 6555 s. 1.2 needs a recipient, no clause on vacant lots (our reading, not settled)

heat_pool_whole.name: Heat demand, whole pool centre or bath
heat_pool_whole.formula: community pool: public floor (public program + public support) x 417-608 kWh/m2 a year (gas, fuel used for heat); warm bath: public floor x 217-507 kWh/m2 a year (353 mid); pool water 150-200 MWh/yr shown as a part, not added
heat_pool_whole.coef: Ontario Broader Public Sector 2024 medians (gas, heated swimming pools; project decision, 11 Nov); KEA-BW 2021 thermal baths, n 6, Table 1 p. 16 (project decision, 15 Nov); provisional

dc_context.name: Data centre in its block (footprints, heights, uses)
dc_context.formula: for each facility on the Data centres map: every building outline within 200 m, its height (Vancouver: City LiDAR 2022 90th percentile where the outline is mostly building cells, else Canada Structures; Edmonton: Canada Structures) and a use class (OpenStreetMap places inside it, else City business licences inside it, else the City zone at its centre); no height = drawn flat, no use = not recorded
dc_context.coef: radius 200 m; heights simplified; use classes homes, shops and food, offices and business, industry and warehouses, schools / health / community, other (zone -> class our reading)

heat_demand_cascade_typ.name: Heat demand, heat cascade spa, aquaponics greenhouse and conservatory biome
heat_demand_cascade_typ.formula: heat cascade: the 40 m2 hot pool's evaporation alone, 70-135 MWh/yr (ASHRAE natatorium method, 38-40 C water, activity factor 1.0 and a field-measured 0.75, covered or not at night), a floor value, spa total not known; aquaponics: greenhouse m2 x 413-583 kWh/m2 a year (fish hall not counted); conservatory: biome m2 x the London benchmark 590 kWh/m2 a year scaled by climate: Vancouver x 1.0-1.3 (judged) = 590-770, Edmonton = Vancouver x 1.90 = 1,120-1,460
heat_demand_cascade_typ.coef: spa: ASHRAE HVAC Applications ch. 6 method, activity factors from Smedegard et al. 2022, opening hours assumed (14 h open); biome: Kew benchmark (our arithmetic) x CMHC 1997 degree-hour ratio; greenhouse: Prairie production greenhouse

row_sky_nothing_above.name: Sky rooms have nothing above (greenhouse, biome, fish hall, pool / spa hall)
row_sky_nothing_above.formula: every greenhouse, biome, fish hall and pool / spa / therapy hall (the definitions' nothing-above rooms) has no storey over it; judged stacking row in the export
row_sky_nothing_above.coef: typology specs (heat cascade, aquaponics, conservatory; pool specs for the halls); roof basis FM DS 5-32 (nothing wet over the data hall)

urban_farm_area.name: Suggested urban farm land on the lot
urban_farm_area.formula: lot outline minus the building (storey 1), the plant yard, every at-grade plant unit and a 3.0 m clearance band round it, the truck court, the truck drive at its own width (also the fire access the layout has) and the public front garden; pieces under 3.0 m wide dropped (0.5 m grid). Shown as a suggestion with its area only: no heat, no yield, not in any total. Vancouver I-2, I-3, M-2 and lots tested as I-2: Urban Farm - Class B is conditional, the permit lasts 1 year and the planting area is capped at 7,000 m² unless relaxed. Edmonton: no current lot shows one (IH and EETC do not list Urban Agriculture; IM would be indoor or rooftop only)
urban_farm_area.coef: 3.0 m clearance round outdoor plant = plant_clearances ("pads ... 3 m clear in front"; chiller ends 2.1 m, a maker claim); 3.0 m minimum width judged (one bed and a path); the homes-within-30 m rule (11.1.2.2) is not applied until an edge-to-edge dwelling test exists

sources.abADR276: Alberta Activities Designation Regulation, Alta Reg 276/2003 (CanLII), Sch. 1 Div. 5 (approval): a waterworks system that is a private utility and draws surface water or groundwater other than high-quality groundwater; Sch. 2 Div. 5 (registration): a private utility using high-quality groundwater, or one that consists solely of a distribution system supplied with potable water from an approved or registered waterworks
sources.abAIDCstrategy2024: Government of Alberta, Alberta's AI Data Centre Strategy: Powering the future of artificial intelligence (Technology and Innovation, Dec 2024, ISBN 978-1-4601-6171-5): three pillars — power capacity (off-grid and grid-connected solutions "that avoid compromising the affordability and reliability of electricity for Albertans"; natural gas with renewables and possibly carbon capture), sustainable cooling ("Alberta will explore innovative ways of capturing and utilizing the heat generated by AI data centres"; cooling strategies that respect the province's water capacity; the Water Act allocation line is in the "Water" section, p. 7, not under the pillars, which start p. 8), economic growth (tax and shared prosperity). An intention, not a requirement — https://open.alberta.ca/publications/albertas-ai-data-centre-strategy
sources.abAltSol2021: Government of Alberta, Notice: Alternative Solutions Guide for Small System Water Reuse and Stormwater Use (Jan 2021; read by the project 16 Oct 2026): reuse 'may require an approved alternative solution' (toilet and urinal flushing and sub-surface irrigation 'may not'; ? one check reads the rest as overstated) from the local authority having jurisdiction; the municipality must support it and oversee monitoring; Water Act / EPEA authorisation from Alberta Environment and Parks may be needed; AEP is 'the lead approving authority' for projects involving more than one property — https://open.alberta.ca/publications/notice-alternative-solutions-guide-small-system-water-reuse-stormwater-use

sources.aesoBYOG2026: AESO, Large Load Integration Phase 2A — Proposed BYOG Process (26 Jun 2026, proposal, not final). Applies to transmission-connected loads asking for 75 MW or more of demand transmission service (DTS), site-aggregated; excludes loads under 75 MW, distribution-connected load and storage. First intake gas-fired generation only, "net new"; tethering ratio: generator output at 25 °C, 40% humidity equals DTS contract capacity. Data centres must show municipal zoning or area-structure-layout approval and accept the data-centre connection requirements. DTS commitment fee $15k/MW (refundable). Bridging before the generator runs: at most 20/30/40% of the DTS request by generator milestone, 1,600 MW across all intakes, up to 3 years; bridging load is fully interruptible, reduced before all other non-firm load to avoid a shortfall, curtailment scheme TBD (pro rata, rotation or combination); suspended for failing to curtail (read from — https://aesoengage.aeso.ca/pre-engagement-phase-ii-large-load-integration

sources.alta117_2026: Data Centre Regulation, Alta Reg 117/2026 under the Electric Utilities Act (King's Printer extract, current as of 9 Jun 2026; the saved file for this id is the catalogue page, the text is under altaReg117). s. 1: data centre includes hosting/cloud, digital asset mining, AI/ML, content delivery. s. 2: "large data centre" = maximum demand directly from the transmission system of 75 MW or more, or a lower threshold the AESO sets for reliability. s. 3: AESO may aggregate integrated data centres on the same or adjacent parcels with the same owner or affiliate. s. 5: a large data centre may be "tethered" to new or added generating units or energy storage able to supply at least its maximum demand, reliably and predictably (the Regulation does not limit the fuel; AESO's first intake does). s. 6: tethered requests processed first. s. 7: AESO may require site control, municipal zoning approvals, financing, permits or water licences. s. 8: no service above the tethered supply. s. 9: bridged service before the supply runs only once the plant is approved by the AUC, max 3 years, AESO may cap each and all bridged loads and suspend for unmet criteria. s. 10: inadequate supply — bridged data centres reduced before all other market participants; mandatory load shed — large data centres reduced before all others. s. 12: review by 31 May 2030, expires 31 May 2035 — https://open.alberta.ca/publications/2026_117

sources.arch_per_gcpsg009hvm: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: RCMP, GCPSG-009 (2022) Security Fencing Considerations Guide, effective 2022-01-27, approved 2022-03-16, page modified 2025-11-03 (official RCMP page; supplements register rcmpGCPSG009 and arch_sec2_gcpsg009b): 8.2 ASTM F2656 'details the requirements for the Hostile Vehicle Mitigation measures'; M30 (K4) 30 mph, M40 (K8) 40 mph, M50 (K12) 50 mph, 15,000 lb vehicle; P1 <1 m, P2 1.1-7 m, P3 7-30 m, P4 ≥30.1 m penetration; 'there is no limit to how far the vehicle can travel past the barrier to be certified'; protection depends on 'the setback and standoff distances' set by a TRA. 9.1 bollards, large planters or rocks as 'larger, more robust vehicular security barriers' where pedestrian traffic is high; back-filled retaining wall as a vehicle barrier; 'Blast pressure falls off with increased standoff'. 9.1, 9.5 ditches and berms. 10.3.2 fences with 'integral crash beams or cables'. 10.6 gate barriers: fixed or movable bollards, wedge/ramp barriers, locking arms, cable barriers; 'the first choice to protect a gate is to limit the approach speed of a vehicle' (curves, chicanes, parallel approach); halving speed cuts impact force to a quarter; gates latch 'approximately every four feet of vertical height'. 10.1 minimum security fence 2.4 m, high security ≥3.6 m. 5 and 9.4: provincial or municipal laws and AHJ height limits may restrict fences. No bollard spacing. — https://rcmp.ca/en/lead-security-agency-physical-security/guidance-and-publications/gcpsg-009-2022-security-fencing-considerations-guide

BCBC and VBBL 3.8.2.8.(4): where WCs are required, 'at least one universal washroom shall be provided in the entrance storey' unless an accessible path leads to one elsewhere (NBC and NBC(AE) 3.8.2.8.(4): 'at least one barrier-free water closet'). sources.arch_pub_nbcDefs: RULE: NBC 2020 Div. A 1.4.1.2 definitions (local text l. 1444, 1477, 1815, 1901, 1983): 'Assembly occupancy (Group A) means the occupancy or the use of a building or part thereof by a gathering of persons for civic, political, travel, religious, social, educational, recreational or like purposes, or for the consumption of food or drink'; 'Building means any structure used or intended for supporting or sheltering any use or occupancy'; 'Mercantile occupancy (Group E) means the occupancy or use of a building or part thereof for the displaying or selling of retail goods, wares or merchandise'; 'Residential occupancy (Group C) means the occupancy or use of a building or part thereof by persons for whom sleeping accommodation is provided but who are not harboured for the purpose of receiving care or treatment and are not involuntarily detained'; 'Suite means a single room or series of rooms of complementary use, operated under a single tenancy ...'. Div. B 3.1.3.2.(2): 'Not more than one suite of residential occupancy shall be contained within a building classified as a Group F, Division 2 major occupancy.' (VBBL 2025 adds 'Except as permitted in Article 3.1.3.4. and 3.1.3.5., and Subsection 11.2.5.' — artist live/work and industrial flex space). 3.3.1.1.(1): each suite (other than business and personal services) separated from adjoining suites by not less than 1 h; 3.3.1.1.(3) exemptions in sprinklered buildings served by public corridors per 3.3.1.4.(4)(b), incl. 'suites of mercantile occupancy'. 3.3.5.4.(1) access from a storage garage to a stair tower or elevator serving occupancies above 'through a vestibule' (3.3.5.7.(4)); 3.3.5.4.(4) garage ventilation per 6.3.1 and 6.9.1.2; 3.3.5.6.(1) storage garage separated from other occupancies by not less than 1.5 h —

sources.arch_up4_ashraeCh52: DESIGN GUIDE (paywalled, single-user licensed copy; US cities only, no Canadian city; supersedes the 2015 edition ashrae2015ch51 for the public edge): 2023 ASHRAE Handbook — HVAC Applications (SI), ch. 52 Snow Melting and Freeze Protection: p. 52.2 entering fluid at most 66 °C (concrete); Table 1 pp. 52.3–52.4 (46 cities, 1982–1993) surface heat flux not exceeded in 99 % of snowfall hours, W/m², Ar = 1 / 0.5 / 0: Fairbanks AK (288 h/yr) 639 / 342 / 152; Great Falls MT (233 h) 869 / 453 / 238; Bismarck ND (158 h) 969 / 520 / 230; Minneapolis–St Paul MN (199 h) 801 / 485 / 355; Spokane WA (144 h) 500 / 300 / 210; Seattle WA (27 h) 647 / 420 / 386; fluxes are at the snow-melting surface only; Table 3 p. 52.6 annual kWh/m² melting + idling at Ar = 1: Fairbanks 62.5 + 1083.9, Great Falls 62.1 + 390.5, Minneapolis 52.1 + 580.3, Seattle 3.8 + 33.1 (back and edge losses not included); Table 4 p. 52.8 general guidance: commercial building sidewalk, steps, wheelchair ramp Ar 1.0 at 90 or 95 %; public building sidewalk Ar 1.0 at 95 %, parking lot 0.5 at 90 %; hospital sidewalk 1.0 at 95 %; p. 52.8 back and edge losses range 4 to 50%, steady-state back losses about 20%, cut to about 1 to 3% by a 50 mm insulation layer; p. 52.9 transient start-up fluxes as much as five times higher, edge losses 15 to 35% of the heat from the element nearest the edge; p. 52.11 standard practice 20 mm pipe or tube at 230 mm centres with at least 50 mm of concrete above, so a 130 mm slab; Table 7 p. 52.11 at mean fluid 55 °C: 440 W/m² at 300 mm, 555 at 230, 665 at 150 mm spacing (plastic pipe); PE limit typically 60 °C, concrete entering water usually below 65 °C or the limit in the relevant standard (e.g., CSA A23); p. 52.12–52.13 with district heating, the snow-melting system may connect to the district's return piping; p. 52.13 fluid ΔT under 17 K; pipe about 50 mm or less below the surface. The 2015 figure of usually 630 to 950 W/m² (back and edge losses included) is not in the 2023 text (text search, our reading)

sources.cec2024ESS: CSA C22.1:24 Canadian Electrical Code, Section 64 (read 19 Oct 2026 and re-read 28 Oct 2026 from the project's licensed copy, March 2024 printing; not stored): published 4 Mar 2024; in force Alberta 1 Apr 2025, BC 4 Mar 2025 (Technical Safety BC, IB-EL 2024-01, 11 Jun 2024) (Alberta Municipal Affairs notice, Apr 2025). Rule 64-1002: battery energy storage over 1 kWh must be certified (Rule 2-024), installed to the manufacturer's instructions, and — except in an electrical equipment vault — not where the floor is more than 23 m above grade or below the lowest level of egress. Rule 64-926: outdoor batteries at least 3 m from a means of egress and 1.5 m from windows, vents and doors, unless evaluated to ANSI/CAN/UL 9540A and installed to the manufacturer's instructions. Rule 64-902: plaque showing the system and its disconnects. Appendix B: the ESS definition does not include a UPS (covered by CSA C22.2 No. 107.3); batteries in general follow Rules 64-800–64-820 (ventilation if they vent gas, access by authorized persons only). 20 kWh / 80 kWh caps apply to residential occupancies only (Rule 64-1100). Section 64 rules are electrical-installation rules; fire-code (NFC/BCFC) ESS provisions not covered; code text not stored, so not independently verifiable ?. Neither Vancouver Fire By-law 14419 (read not stored ?) nor Edmonton Fire Rescue Services Bylaw 15309 (consolidated 1 Jan 2025, read) has battery or fuel provisions —

sources.lot_edm_5130: RULE: City of Edmonton Zoning Bylaw 20001, s. 5.130 Unique Lot Conditions (as adopted, PDF 3 Jan 2024; PDF p. 882, printed p. 881). '1. On Corner Sites consisting of more than 1 Lot, the Front Lot Line of the Site is the same as the Front Lot Line of the Corner Lot. 2. If the 2 Lot lines of a Corner Site Abutting a Street are equal in length, the location of the Front Lot Line of the Site must be determined by the Development Planner. ... 3. Despite Subsections 1 and 2 and the definition of Front Lot Line, the Development Planner may determine that a Corner Site has additional Front Lot Lines other than what is required. ... 4. Double Fronting Sites must have 2 Front Lot Lines. 5. To determine if a Lot or Site along a curved Street is a Corner Lot or Corner Site, the Development Planner must take into account the angle where the lines tangent to each of the two endpoints of the curved Lot or Site intersect. 6. The corner of a Corner Lot or Corner Site is the point on the curved Lot line(s) that is closest to the two intersecting tangent lines described in Subsection 6.' (sic: subsection 6 refers to itself; read as subsection 5). Industrial zones set setbacks by what a lot line abuts, not by front, side or rear: IM s. 2.130 Table 4.1 'Minimum Setback Abutting a Street 3.0 m', 'Abutting an Alley 0 m', 'Abutting a Site in a non-industrial Zone 6.0 m', 'Abutting a Site in an industrial Zone 0 m' (PDF p. 112).
sources.lot_edm_820_lines: RULE: City of Edmonton Zoning Bylaw 20001, s. 8.20 General Definitions (as adopted, PDF 3 Jan 2024, OCR text; printed page = PDF page - 1). 'Abut means immediately contiguous to or physically touching. When used in reference to a Lot or a Site, Abut means that the Lot or Site physically touches another Lot, Site, or piece of land, and shares a Lot line with it.' and 'Alley means a narrow roadway primarily intended to give access to the rear of buildings and parcels of land.' (p. 1021). 'Corner Lot means a Lot that is: a. located at the intersection of 2 Streets, if the angle of the intersection is less than 135 degrees; or b. Abutting a Street that is curved less than 135 degrees where it Abuts the Lot, in compliance with Section 5.130.' (p. 1027). 'Corner Site means a Site where at least 1 Lot is a Corner Lot.' (p. 1028). 'Double Fronting Site means a Site that Abuts 2 Streets that are parallel or nearly parallel.' (p. 1029). 'Flanking Side Lot Line means a Lot line, other than a Front Lot Line, that Abuts a Street on a Corner Site.' (p. 1032). 'Flanking Street means a Street Abutting a Flanking Side Lot Line.' (p. 1033). 'Front Lot Line means: a. the Lot line separating a Lot from an Abutting Street; b. in the case of a Corner Lot, the Front Lot Line is the shorter of the Lot lines Abutting a Street; c. in the case of a Corner Lot formed by a curved Street, the Front Lot Line is the shorter of the 2 Lot line segments between the point determined to be the actual corner in Section 5.130, and the 2 points at the endpoints of that Lot line; or d. in the case of a Reverse Housing development, ...' (p. 1035). 'Interior Lot means a Lot other than a Corner Lot.' and 'Interior Side Lot Line means the Lot line other than a Front Lot Line, Flanking Side Lot Line or Rear Lot Line.' (p. 1039). 'Rear Lot Line means: a) the Lot line that is furthest from and opposite the Front Lot Line; or b) where there is no such Lot line, the point of intersection of any Lot lines that are furthest from and opposite the Front Lot Line.' (p. 1047). 'Setback means the distance that a development, or a specified portion of a development, must be from a Lot line. A Setback is not a Yard. ...' (p. 1051). 'Site means an area of land consisting of 1 or more Abutting Lots.' (p. 1052). 'Street means any public roadway other than an Alley ...' (p. 1055). Not found in 8.20: an angle for "nearly parallel" (?), any angle for "opposite" (?), a panhandle or flag-lot definition (?).
sources.lot_van_exterior_side: RULE: City of Vancouver district schedules (June 2026; local copies, van_zdb_i3, van_zdb_fc2): on a corner site the exterior side yard takes the front yard. I-2 s. 3.2.2.13 (sub-area B only, p. 17): 'on a corner site, the exterior side yard and side setback requirements are the same as the front yard and front setback requirements in this section 3.2.' I-3 s. 3.1.2.15 (p. 13): 'in the case of a corner site, the exterior side yard and side setback requirements are the same as the front yard and front setback requirements in this section 3.1.' FC-2 ss. 3.1.2.10 (sub-areas A, B; p. 12), 3.2.2.10 (C1; p. 15), 3.3.2.10 (C2, D; p. 19), 3.4.2.10 (E; p. 22): 'in the case of a corner site, the exterior side yard width and side setback requirements are the same as the front yard depth and front setback requirements ...'. I-2 outside sub-area B (s. 3.1.2.2, p. 11): side yard only where it 'adjoins a site located in any R ... district, without the intervention of a lane'; no exterior side yard clause found. I-1C: no corner or exterior side yard clause found (?).
sources.lot_van_s10_frontage: RULE: City of Vancouver Zoning and Development By-law, Section 10 General Regulations (footers May 2026; local copy). 10.4.1 (p. 3): development on a corner site in an RA, RT (except RT-7, RT-9) or C-1 district 'or as required in other districts, that has a site at its rear that fronts on the flanking street' must give the principal building a setback from the flanking street of at least half the required front yard of the site at its rear (not over the greater of 3.7 m or the district side yard). 10.6.1 (p. 3): 'The building placement and design of all buildings on a double fronting site located in any district, other than an M or I district, requires the approval of the Director of Planning.' 10.25.1 (p. 11): 'Where an area of land does not abut a street and therefore is not defined as a site, development may be permitted by the Director of Planning ...'. 10.26.1 (p. 12): 'The frontage of any site having more than 1 boundary on a street is: (a) where street boundary lengths are equal, as determined by the Director of Planning; (b) in the case of a corner site, the shortest boundary abutting on a street, or as otherwise determined by the Director of Planning; and (c) where a site is composed of more than 1 lot, the shortest boundary abutting on a street, or as otherwise determined by the Director of Planning.' Not found in Section 10: a rule for irregular, notched or panhandle sites (?).
sources.lot_van_s2_lines: RULE: City of Vancouver Zoning and Development By-law, Section 2 Definitions (footers June 2026; local copy, same file as van3575s2). 'Corner Site: A site located at the intersection or junction of 2 or more streets.' (p. 9). 'Double Fronting Site: A site abutting 2 parallel or approximately parallel streets.' (p. 11). 'Exterior Side Yard: That portion of a corner site extending from the front yard to the rear yard and lying between the side property line adjacent to the flanking street and the closest side of the principal building.' (p. 14). 'Front Yard: That part of the site lying between the ultimate front property line and the front of the principal building, extending across the full width of the site.' (p. 17). 'Lane: A public thoroughfare or way not more than 10.1 m in width that affords only a secondary means of access to a site, at the side or rear.' (p. 22). 'Rear Yard: That part of the site lying between the ultimate rear property line and the rear of the principal building or rear building, extending across the full width of the site.' (p. 33). 'Side Yard: The part of the site extending from the front yard to the rear yard and lying between the ultimate side property line and the closest side of the principal building.' (p. 42). 'Site: An area of land consisting of 1 or more adjoining parcels or lots abutting on a street not being a lane ...' (p. 43). 'Ultimate Property Line: The property line that results when an anticipated or partially dedicated lane or street abuts a site, and that becomes the property boundary for the purposes of measuring required yards.' (p. 46). Diagrams "Site Configurations" (p. 43: corner, double fronting, corner double fronting) and "Site Yards" (p. 49: F at the street, S at the two sides, R at the lane). Not found in Section 2: any definition of front, rear or side property line (?), any rule for irregular, notched or panhandle sites (?), any angle for "approximately parallel" (?).

sources.nfpa37_2024: STANDARD (US, benchmark; paywalled, read on NFPA Free Access): NFPA 37, Installation and Use of Stationary Combustion Engines and Gas Turbines, 2024 edition (pp. 37-8 to 37-12): 4.1.1.1 engines readily accessible (NFPA 37's defined term) for maintenance, repair and firefighting; 4.1.1.2 air supply designed so that flue gases are not drawn in from stacks or flues; 4.1.2.1.1 engine rooms within structures: walls, floors and ceilings rated at least 1 hour; 4.1.2.1.4 attached engine rooms: common wall at least 1 h; 4.1.2.1.5 openings with self-closing fire doors or dampers to match; 4.1.2.2.2 dedicated detached structures at least 1.5 m (5 ft) from openings in walls and from structures with combustible walls, no minimum where the exposing or exposed wall is 1 h or the detached structure is sprinklered; 4.1.3 on roofs: 4.1.3.1 at least 1.5 m from any openings in the walls of structures; 4.1.3.2 1.5 m from combustible walls unless 1 h (4.1.3.2.1), a fire test (4.1.3.2.2) or engineering calculations (4.1.3.2.3); 4.1.3.3 oil containment curb or dike holding the full lube-oil or fuel capacity; 4.1.3.4 noncombustible surface 300 mm beyond the engine and dike; 4.1.4 outdoors: 4.1.4.1 1.5 m (5 ft) minimum from openings in structure walls (no exceptions); 4.1.4.2 1.5 m from structures having combustible walls, except 4.1.4.2.1 (structure within 1.5 m rated at least 1 h), 4.1.4.2.2 (fire test) or 4.1.4.2.2.3 (? numbering) (calculations) — the exceptions apply to combustible walls only, not to openings (our reading of the clause structure); 6.3.2.2 fuel tanks not in a room of their own at most 2,500 L; larger tanks in a room per 6.3.5 or 6.3.6 (read later, see below); 6.3.2.3 aggregate in a structure at most 5,000 L unless the excess is in such a room; 6.3.2.2.1 and 6.3.2.3.1 any size within engine rooms if engineered with fire detection, suppression and containment. Roof installation is permitted by NFPA 37 (contrast FM Global 5-32 2.6.4.3.1).

US standard, edition not stated; US reference figure only, not a BC/AB rule. Vancouver bulletin 2000-015 points to CSA C282 (a separate source, not checked; C282 paywalled, not read) — https://ncosfm.gov/fuel-gas/3013-3rd-party-listing-requirement-generator-clearance-reduction-1/open
sources.nfpa75_2024: STANDARD (US, benchmark; paywalled, read on NFPA Free Access): NFPA 75, Fire Protection of Information Technology Equipment, 2024 edition: 6.1.1 the ITE area in a fully sprinklered building or a Type I or II (noncombustible) building; 6.1.3 fire-resistance-rated construction separates the ITE area from other occupancies in the building, atria and other open spaces included; 6.1.3.1 the ITE room separated from other occupancies in the ITE area; 6.1.3.2 rating matched to the exposure, at least 1 hour for both; 6.1.3.3 enclosures from structural floor to structural floor above or roof; 6.1.3.4 doors: 2 h construction, 1½ h doors; 1 h construction, ¾ h doors; 6.1.3.6 separation may instead be set by a documented fire risk assessment (Ch. 4); 6.3.1 the ITE area not above, below or next to areas or structures with hazardous processes unless approved protection is provided; 6.3.2 ITE area access limited to authorized persons; 6.3.3 floors under ITE able to remove leaks (drains or containment with pumps); 6.3.3.2 leak detection under raised floors where liquids are piped in; 6.6.2 pass-throughs or windows in rated construction need fire-rated shutters, a service-counter fire door or fire-rated windows, closing automatically on smoke or fire (6.6.2.1), rated at least as the wall (6.6.2.2); 6.6.3 fire and smoke dampers on ducts through rated construction; 7.1.1 the ITE room holds only ITE and support equipment; 7.3.4 no combustible storage in battery rooms; 9.1.1 ITE rooms in a sprinklered building are sprinklered; 4.2.3–4.2.4 the fire risk assessment covers life safety of occupants of adjacent spaces and the general public, and all adjacent exposures. Applies where ITE is installed in rooms of strategic importance (A.1.3.2).
sources.nfpa855_2026: STANDARD (US, benchmark; read on NFPA Free Access): NFPA 855, Installation of Stationary Energy Storage Systems, 2026 edition: 1.3 and Table 1.3 apply above 20 kWh of lithium-ion per fire area or outdoor installation (lead-acid 70 kWh); UPS exemptions (UPS listed to UL 1778: 9.2.1.1(3), 9.3.1(6), 9.5.1.4(6), 9.7.2.2(6)) cover only lead-acid, aqueous nickel-based and aqueous metal-air batteries, so a lithium-ion UPS is not exempt (our reading of the clause wording); 9.5.1.1 groups of at most 50 kWh each; 9.5.1.2 groups 0.9 m (3 ft) from other groups and from walls; 9.5.1.3 larger groups or less spacing if fire testing (9.2) shows it; 9.4.1.1 a dedicated-use ESS building holds only energy storage or grid/communications equipment, no other occupancy, admin areas at most 10 % of the storey behind 2 h fire barriers; 9.6.1.2.1.1 in occupied work centres ESSs are permitted in the same room as the equipment they serve; 9.6.1.2.1.2 in a noncombustible locked cabinet unless in an equipment room accessible only to authorized personnel; 9.6.1.2.2.1 not in sleeping rooms or spaces opening directly into them; outdoors (9.6.2.7.1): at least 3 m (10 ft) from lot lines, public ways, buildings, stored combustibles, hazardous materials and other exposures, reducible to 0.9 m with a 1 h freestanding exterior barrier (9.6.2.7.1.1), a noncombustible wall without openings of matching rating (9.6.2.7.1.2), fire testing (9.6.2.7.1.3) or a 2 h-rated ESS enclosure (9.6.2.7.1.5); 9.6.2.7.1.6 ESS exhaust outlets at least 4.57 m (15 ft) from HVAC intakes, windows, doors, loading docks and other openings, not directed onto egress, walkways or travel paths; 9.6.2.7.1.7 at least 3 m from any means of egress; 9.6.2.1.1 3 m cleared of combustible vegetation; 9.6.2.6 no occupied work centres in outdoor installations; rooftops (9.6.3.1.1.2): 1.5 m (or the equipment height) from the roof edge, 3 m from the fire service access point, 1.5 m service walkways, standpipe outlet, no open racks; 9.6.3.1.3.1 rooftop ESSs 3 m from other buildings, lot lines, public ways and parking; 9.7.1 smoke or thermal-image detection; 9.7.2.1 suppression per 4.9; 9.7.3.1 a permanent water supply.

sources.rule_codeLevel: DECISION:, how far the code checks go. Check the big moves: use and approval; envelope (height, floor area, yards, depth, flood construction level); separations (2 h between data centre and public programs, nothing wet over the hall); exits (two per zone, travel 45 m, exits apart, dead ends 6 m, egress doors for rooms over 60 people, exit width by load, no public exits through data-centre space or plant yards); room minimum area and width; washroom counts by load (VBBL 3.7.2.2) and one universal washroom per hub; loading counts; plant clearances; step-free entry. Not checked (detailed design): fixture layouts, accessible stalls, door swings, grab bars, edge-vs-centre measurement and other sub-0.5 m refinements, finishes, hardware, signage, lighting, intake and exhaust placement. Tolerance: a result within 0.5 m (or 5 %) of a limit is 'tight: check in design', not re-planned; re-layout only when a big-move rule fails by more. A decision, not a source: no trust rating (n/a).

sources.weyburnC282: SECONDARY (fire department summary of a paywalled standard): Weyburn Fire Department, 'Emergency Power Systems Requirements' (undated; posted Apr 2024 ?), citing CSA C282 'Emergency Electrical Power Supply for Buildings': a thorough monthly test of the emergency electrical power, running the set at no less than 30% of rated load for 60 minutes with transfer switches operated under load; an annual 2-hour full-load test; weekly tests for health-care facilities. Applies to emergency (life-safety) power systems; whether a data centre's standby generators for IT load fall under C282 is not stated (?; Vancouver bulletin 2000-015 points emergency generator rooms to C282). CSA C282 itself not read (paywalled) — https://weyburn.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/Emergency-Power-Systems-Requirements.pdf

sources.whiteSpacePrecedents2026: PRECEDENT CHECK (operator claims, trust 50):, white space per MW of IT for air-cooled, about 7-8 kW a rack halls: 23 precedents from operator pages and planning documents (sources S1-S22 in that file), each opened 23 Nov 2026; plant check against published generator, UPS and cooling capacity; median of the 9 plant-checked halls about 740 m2 a MW, with 620 and 830 as the low and high cases (main, project decision). Operators measure white space differently (about +-20 %); advertised MW overstates what small sites' plant carries.
